definition_zh: 花费；度过；消耗
definition_en: to use money to buy things, to pass time in a place or way, or to use up energy
core_image: 收银台上硬币一枚枚被推出去，旁边日历上的日子也一页页翻过
scene: 他们在海边度过了整个周末。 They spent the whole weekend at the beach.
sceneCN: 这里 spend 是「度过」（第 2 个义项）；句意：他们在海边度过了整个周末。

derivatives.zh: 开支；花费
花钱的人
挥霍者

senses.title: To pay out money
senses.definition: to use money to buy something
senses.definitionCN: 用钱购买东西
senses.example: She spent fifty pounds on the coat.
senses.exampleCN: 她花了五十英镑买那件大衣。
senses.why: This is the oldest and most common sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老也最常见的含义。

senses.title: To pass time
senses.definition: to pass time in a particular way or place
senses.definitionCN: 以特定方式或在特定地点度过时间
senses.example: They spent the whole weekend at the beach.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在海边度过了整个周末。
senses.why: Time is treated like money that is paid out.
senses.whyCN: 时间被当作花出去的钱。

senses.title: To use up energy
senses.definition: to use up energy or effort on something
senses.definitionCN: 在某事上耗尽精力或努力
senses.example: He spent all his energy on the project.
senses.exampleCN: 他把全部精力都花在这个项目上。
senses.why: Energy can be spent like money and time.
senses.whyCN: 精力也能像金钱和时间一样被花掉。

intro.en: Spend came from Latin expendere, to weigh out money, through Old English.
intro.cn: spend 经古英语来自拉丁语 expendere，意为称出钱来支付。

items.en: Expendere meant to weigh out and pay money.
items.cn: expendere 意为称出并支付钱款。

items.en: Spendan meant to pay out or use up.
items.cn: spendan 意为支付或耗尽。

items.en: Spend came to mean passing time as well.
items.cn: spend 也开始表示度过时间。

items.en: Spending became the word for household costs.
items.cn: spending 成为表示家庭开支的词。

items.en: Spend energy extended it beyond money.
items.cn: spend energy 把它扩展到金钱之外。

note.en: Spend is compared with look-alike words and verbs of using resources.
note.cn: 把 spend 与形近词以及表示使用资源的动词作比较。

entries.definition: rate of movement
entries.definitionCN: 速度

entries.definition: to write letters in order
entries.definitionCN: 拼写

entries.definition: to make something go somewhere
entries.definitionCN: 寄送

entries.definition: to give money for something
entries.definitionCN: 支付

entries.definition: to consume for a purpose
entries.definitionCN: 使用

entries.definition: to go through a period of time
entries.definitionCN: 度过

normalIntro.en: To spend is to let something valuable flow out of your hands.
normalIntro.cn: spend 就是让有价值的东西从手中流走。

normal.en: They spent the whole weekend at the beach.
normal.cn: 他们在海边度过了整个周末。

normal.en: She spent fifty pounds on the coat.

normal.en: He spent all his energy on the project.

normal.en: We spent the night in a small hotel.

normal.en: Learn to spend wisely.

abstract.en: Time is the only currency no one can earn back.
abstract.cn: 时间是人唯一赚不回来的货币。

abstract.en: What we spend shows what we value.
abstract.cn: 我们把钱花在哪，就说明我们看重什么。

abstract.en: A day spent well is never a payment.
abstract.cn: 过得好的一天，从来不是一笔支出。

dict_mnemonic.text: spend 源自拉丁语 expendere（称出钱款），表示「花费」，也可指「度过时间」和「消耗精力」；spending 是「开支」，spender 是「花钱的人」，spendthrift 是「挥霍者」。

root: 来自拉丁语 expendere（称量、支付），经古英语 spendan 进入英语，核心义为付出金钱，后扩展到时间与精力的消耗。

sensesIntro.en: Spend means to pay out money, to pass time, or to use up energy.
sensesIntro.cn: spend 指付出金钱、度过时间，或消耗精力。

core.en: Letting valuable things flow away.
core.cn: 让有价值的东西流走。

branches.en: Coins cross a counter into another hand.
branches.cn: 硬币越过柜台，进入另一只手。

branches.en: A family walks the shore until evening.
branches.cn: 一家人沿着海岸走到傍晚。

branches.en: A worker pours the last of his strength into a task.
branches.cn: 工人把最后的力气投进工作。

branches.en: Money and time are both counted out and given away.
branches.cn: 金钱与时间都被数着交出去。

branches.en: Time and energy pass through the same open hand.
branches.cn: 时间与精力穿过同一只张开的手。

intro.en: Spend forms nouns for money use and for people.
intro.cn: spend 构成表示用钱和用钱者的名词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root is expendere, to weigh out and pay.
latinIntro.cn: 其拉丁词根是 expendere（称出并支付）。

definition_zh: 证明；证实；结果是；检验；证明自己
definition_en: to show that something is true by evidence, to turn out to be a particular way, or to test something in practice
core_image: 一叠材料被推到桌上，最后一页的印章让所有疑问停了下来
scene: 争论一直持续到深夜，直到有人把当年的登记簿翻到那一页，指着上面的签名。 The old register proved that the land had belonged to her family.
sceneCN: 这里表示「证明、证实」（第 1 个义项：用证据使某件事确定为真）；句意为那本旧登记簿证明了这块地一直属于她家。

derivatives.zh: 与 prove 同源的名词，经古法语 preove 而来，义为「证据；证明」
由过去分词转成的形容词，义为「已被证实的；经考验的」
由 prove 加 -able 构成，义为「可证明的」
由 prove 加否定前缀 dis- 构成，义为「证明……有误；驳倒」

senses.title: To show that something is true
senses.definition: to give facts, documents or tests that make it certain that something is true or real
senses.definitionCN: 拿出事实、文件或检验，使某事被确定为真或确实存在
senses.example: The fingerprints proved that he had been in the room.
senses.exampleCN: 指纹证明他曾在那间屋子里。
senses.why: Latin probare meant to test something and find it good, so proving starts as an examination that ends in a verdict rather than as a mere opinion.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 probare 意为检验某物并认定它站得住，所以「证明」起初是一场检验，最后落成判决，而不只是看法。

senses.title: To turn out to be a particular thing
senses.definition: to be found, after events have unfolded, to have a certain quality, often one that was not expected
senses.definitionCN: 事情展开之后，被发现具有某种性质，且常是原先没料到的
senses.example: The shortcut proved longer than the road we usually take.
senses.exampleCN: 那条近路结果比我们常走的路还远。
senses.why: Once a test is finished, the result simply is what it is; English lets the verb carry that outcome, so a thing can prove difficult without anyone proving it.
senses.whyCN: 检验结束之后，结果就摆在那里；英语让这个动词直接承担结果，于是事物本身可以 prove difficult，而不需要谁去证明它。

senses.title: To test something in order to learn its quality
senses.definition: to try a method, a weapon or a machine under real conditions to see whether it works
senses.definitionCN: 在真实条件下试用某种方法、武器或机器，看它是否管用
senses.example: The engineers proved the new pump under heavy load before selling it.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师在重载下检验了新水泵，然后才出售。
senses.why: This is the oldest layer made visible: before a thing can be proved true, it has to be put to the test, and the verb still names that trial.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老那层意思的直接显现：在被证明为真之前，东西得先经受检验，而这个动词至今仍指那场试验。

senses.title: To show one's own ability or courage
senses.definition: to show through action that one deserves a place, a role or respect
senses.definitionCN: 通过行动表明自己配得上某个位置、角色或尊重
senses.example: She proved herself in her first month on the night shift.
senses.exampleCN: 她在上夜班的第一个月就证明了自己。
senses.why: When the thing being proved is the speaker, the test and the result collapse into one act, which is why English says prove oneself rather than adding true as well.
senses.whyCN: 当被证明的对象是说话者本人时，检验与结果合成一个动作，所以英语说 prove oneself，不再额外加 true。

intro.en: Prove descends from a Latin verb that meant to test and to judge as good; English keeps both the trial and the verdict, and later let the word also mean to turn out.
intro.cn: prove 源自一个意为「检验并判定为好」的拉丁动词；英语同时保留了检验与判决，后来又让它表示「结果如何」。

items.en: Probus meant upright, honest and of good quality, said of a person or a thing that had been checked.
items.cn: probus 意为正直、诚实、品质良好，用于经过查验的人或物。

items.en: Probare meant to test something and to approve it as good, joining the act of examining to the verdict.
items.cn: probare 意为检验某物并认可它合格，把查验的动作与判决连在一起。

items.en: The participle probatus described what had stood the test, and it is the shape behind the English word.
items.cn: 分词 probatus 描述经住了检验的东西，是英语这个词背后的形式。

items.en: Old French prover meant to test and to demonstrate, and it brought the verb into English.
items.cn: 古法语 prover 意为检验、论证，把这个动词带进英语。

items.en: English split the old family: proof became the noun for the evidence, while prove kept the testing and added the modern sense of turning out.
items.cn: 英语把这一族拆开：proof 成为表示证据的名词，prove 留住检验，又添上「结果是」这层现代用法。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin verb of testing, including the noun English split off from it; the second group gathers verbs for showing something to be true or false.
note.cn: 第一组共用表示「检验」的拉丁动词，包括英语从它分出去的名词；第二组收表示「表明真假」的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for evidence that settles a question, split off from the same French form.
entries.definitionCN: 能定下疑问的证据名词，与动词同出法语形式。

entries.definition: The participle used as an adjective for something already shown to be true.
entries.definitionCN: 分词转作形容词，指已被证实的东西。

entries.definition: Likely to be true, from the same Latin verb of testing and approving.
entries.definitionCN: 很可能是真的，出自同一个表示检验与认可的拉丁动词。

entries.definition: To investigate closely, originally to test a wound or a surface.
entries.definitionCN: 仔细查究，原指探查伤口或表面。

entries.definition: To show clearly by argument or by an example.
entries.definitionCN: 用论证或实例清楚地表明。

entries.definition: To check that something is true or accurate.
entries.definitionCN: 核查某事是否真实、准确。

entries.definition: To show that a fact is certain, often in a formal way.
entries.definitionCN: 表明某事实确凿，常较正式。

entries.definition: To be discovered to be a particular way in the end.
entries.definitionCN: 最终被发现是某种样子。

normalIntro.en: The family keeps the picture of a test that ends in a verdict: something is put under pressure, and the result is then allowed to speak.
normalIntro.cn: 这一族词保留着「检验之后落成判决」的画面：某物被压上压力，然后让结果自己说话。

normal.en: Probare is to test and to approve, so prove carries a courtroom inside it: first the examination, then the finding.
normal.cn: probare 既是检验也是认可，所以 prove 里装着一间法庭：先审，再判。

normal.en: Proof is the same family seen as a thing rather than an act, which is why a proof is handed over while a prove is performed.
normal.cn: proof 是同一族词被看成「物」而不是「动作」，所以 proof 可以递过去，prove 只能被执行。

normal.en: Probable keeps the approving half: what is probable has enough testing behind it to be believed.
normal.cn: probable 保留了「认可」的那一半：很可能的事，背后已有足够的检验让人相信。

normal.en: Disprove adds dis- to the front, so the test now ends in rejection instead of approval.
normal.cn: disprove 在前面加 dis-，于是检验以否定而不是认可收场。

normal.en: Prove looks like protect because both start with pro-, but probare means to test, and there is no covering anywhere in it.
normal.cn: prove 与 protect 都以 pro- 开头，但 probare 意为检验，其中没有任何「遮盖」。

abstract.en: A proof is a test that has stopped being a question, and the verb marks the moment that change happens.
abstract.cn: 证据是一场不再提问的检验，而这个动词标出的正是那变化发生的瞬间。

abstract.en: One word covers testing, judging and turning out because all three are stages of the same examination.
abstract.cn: 同一个词兼指检验、判定与结果，因为三者是同一场查验的不同阶段。

abstract.en: To prove something is to accept that it might fail, which is why the word is as much about risk as about certainty.
abstract.cn: 证明某物，就是承认它有可能失败，所以这个词既关乎确定，也关乎冒险。

examples.en: The video proved that the door had been locked all night.
examples.cn: 录像证明那扇门整夜都锁着。

examples.en: The task proved harder than anyone expected.
examples.cn: 这项任务结果比任何人预料的都难。

examples.en: He worked two extra shifts to prove himself.
examples.cn: 他多上了两个班来证明自己。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普如夫」——像「扑过去捋清楚」，把乱糟糟的事捋到只剩一条真相；记住 prove 是证明。

root: 拉丁语 probus（正直的、品质良好的）→ probare（检验、验后认可）→ probatus（经住检验的），经古法语 prover 进入英语；同族词还有 proof、probable、probe、probity。注意 prove 与 protect 都带前缀 pro-，但 prove 的词根是 probare（检验），protect 的词根是 tegere（覆盖），两者只是前缀相同。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a test ending in a verdict; the senses run from proving a fact, through the result of events, to testing a thing and proving oneself.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「以检验收尾的判定」；义项从证明一个事实，到事情的结果，再到检验一物与证明自己。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stack of papers pushed across a table, and a stamp on the last page that ends every doubt.
core.cn: 核心意象：一叠材料被推到桌上，最后一页的印章让所有疑问停下来。

branches.en: a register opened to the page with the signature
branches.cn: 登记簿翻到有签名的那一页

branches.en: a short cut that turns out longer
branches.cn: 结果反而更远的那条近路

branches.en: a pump running under heavy load
branches.cn: 重载下运转的水泵

branches.en: a new worker taking the hardest shift
branches.cn: 新人接下最难的班次

branches.en: one word for examining and for concluding
branches.cn: 同一个词既指查验也指结论

intro.en: A Latin adjective of good quality, the verb of testing built on it, and the French and English forms that split into proof and prove hold the word together.
intro.cn: 表示品质良好的拉丁形容词、由它构成的「检验」动词，以及分化为 proof 与 prove 的法语、英语形式，共同支撑这个词。

latinIntro.en: Probus, probare and probatus are the reliable Latin cognates, and proof is the same family seen as a noun.
latinIntro.cn: probus、probare 与 probatus 是可靠的同源词；proof 则是同一族词被看成名词的样子。

definition_zh: 比赛；火柴；相配的人或物；相配；匹配；比得上
definition_en: a contest between two sides, a small stick that makes fire when struck, a person or thing that fits another, or to fit with and be equal to something
core_image: 细木划过盒面迸出火星，两队人也正好站到对面
scene: 体育馆的看台上坐满了人，双方球员在场地两端排开，裁判把哨子放到嘴边。 The final match began under a grey sky, with the crowd already on its feet.
sceneCN: 这里 match 是「比赛」（第 1 个义项：两队或两人按规则分胜负的较量）；句意为决赛在灰蒙蒙的天空下开始，看台上的人已经站了起来。图中可辨识物件：满座的看台、两端排开的球员、裁判的哨子。

pos.zh: 比赛；火柴；相配的人或物

derivatives.zh: 由 match 与 box 复合而成，义为「火柴盒」
由表示「错误」的前缀 mis- 加 match 构成，义为「不匹配；错配」
由 match 与 maker 复合而成，义为「媒人；撮合者」
由表示「不」的前缀 un- 加 matched 构成，义为「无可匹敌的」

senses.title: A contest between two sides
senses.definition: a contest in which two people or teams compete under rules to win
senses.definitionCN: 两人或两队为争胜而按规则进行的较量
senses.example: The final match began under a grey sky.
senses.exampleCN: 决赛在灰蒙蒙的天空下开始了。
senses.why: The pairing sense is older than the contest: a match was first a pair set against each other, and only later the event they played.
senses.whyCN: 配对义比比赛义更早：match 起初是被摆到彼此对面的一对，后来才指这一对人所进行的赛事。

senses.title: A small stick that makes fire
senses.definition: a small piece of wood or paper with a treated head that makes fire when struck
senses.definitionCN: 带药头的小木梗或纸梗，摩擦时起火
senses.example: He struck a match and the lamp caught at once.
senses.exampleCN: 他划着一根火柴，灯立刻亮了。
senses.why: The fire sense comes from a different word altogether, one that named the wick of a lamp before it named a stick you strike.
senses.whyCN: 「火柴」这个义项来自另一个完全不同的词：它先指灯芯，后来才指手里用来划的那种小梗。

senses.title: A person or thing that fits another
senses.definition: a person or thing that is exactly suitable for another and forms a good pair with it
senses.definitionCN: 与另一个人或物恰好合适、能配成一对的人或物
senses.example: The two of them are a good match in temperament.
senses.exampleCN: 他们两人在性情上是很好的一对。
senses.why: Old English gemæcca meant a mate or an equal, so suitability was built into the word before it ever meant a game.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 gemæcca 本就指配偶或地位相当的人，所以「合适」这层意思在它指比赛之前就已经长在词里了。

senses.title: To fit together with something else
senses.definition: to be the same as, or to fit together with, something else
senses.definitionCN: 与另一事物相同，或彼此契合、对得上
senses.example: The curtains match the colour of the old walls.
senses.exampleCN: 窗帘的颜色和老墙很相配。
senses.why: If two things form a match, the verb names the act of bringing them into that pair, which is why colours, names and records can all be matched.
senses.whyCN: 若两样东西构成一对，动词便表示把它们配成那一对的动作，所以颜色、名字与记录都能 match。

senses.title: To be equal in strength or quality
senses.definition: to be equal in strength, speed or quality to someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 在力量、速度或水准上与某人某物相当，不落下风
senses.example: No one in the class could match her speed at the bench.
senses.exampleCN: 班上没有人在实验台前比得上她的速度。
senses.why: A match is also an equal opponent, so the verb means placing yourself beside that equal and finding nothing missing.
senses.whyCN: match 也指势均力敌的对手，所以动词表示把自己摆到那个对手旁边，发现并不缺什么。

intro.en: Match is two words that came to look alike: one Germanic word for a pair or an equal, and one Latin word for a lamp wick that became the fire stick.
intro.cn: match 是两个后来长得一模一样的词：一个日耳曼词表示「一对、地位相当」，一个拉丁词表示「灯芯」，后者变成了火柴。

items.en: Gemæcca meant a mate, a companion or an equal, and it named the second half of a pair rather than a game.
items.cn: gemæcca 指配偶、同伴或地位相当的人，命名的是成对中的另一半，而不是一场比赛。

items.en: Myxa meant the wick of a lamp; it passed through Greek into Latin before it named anything that could be struck.
items.cn: myxa 指灯芯；它经希腊语进入拉丁语，那时还不指任何能划着的东西。

items.en: Old French meiche named a wick, and English borrowed it for the cord that carried fire to gunpowder and then for the little stick.
items.cn: 古法语 meiche 指灯芯，英语借它来指把火引到火药的引线，后来又指那根小木梗。

items.en: Middle English used matchen for pairing and meiche for the wick, and the two forms slowly merged in sound and spelling.
items.cn: 中古英语用 matchen 表示配对，用 meiche 表示灯芯，两种形式在读音与拼写上慢慢合流。

items.en: Modern English keeps both lines, so one word now covers a game, a small fire, a fitting partner and the act of equalling another.
items.cn: 现代英语把两条线索都留着，于是一个词同时覆盖比赛、小火、相配的伴侣，以及与他人相等这一动作。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers compounds and derivatives built on match plus one close spelling; the near group gathers words for contests, fitting partners and equals.
note.cn: 形近组收由 match 构成的复合词与派生词，外加一个拼写相近的词；近义组收表示比赛、合适的伴侣与地位相当者的词。

entries.definition: A small box for holding matches.
entries.definitionCN: 装火柴的小盒子；由 match 与 box 复合而成。

entries.definition: A pairing that does not fit well.
entries.definitionCN: 配得不好的组合；由表示「错误」的前缀 mis- 加 match 构成。

entries.definition: A person who arranges marriages or brings people together.
entries.definitionCN: 安排婚事或撮合别人的人；由 match 与 maker 复合而成。

entries.definition: To walk with regular steps, or the third month; the spelling is close but the source is different.
entries.definitionCN: 齐步走；也指三月；只是拼写相近，词源不同，与 match 无关。

entries.definition: A competition in which people try to win.
entries.definitionCN: 人们争胜的比赛。

entries.definition: A single occasion of play under rules.
entries.definitionCN: 按规则进行的一场游戏或比赛。

entries.definition: A person or thing that corresponds to another.
entries.definitionCN: 与另一方相对应的人或物。

entries.definition: A person of the same ability or rank as another.
entries.definitionCN: 能力或地位与他人相当的人。

normalIntro.en: Two histories meet in one spelling: a Germanic word for a pair and a Latin word for a wick, and the family keeps returning to pairing, fire and equal standing.
normalIntro.cn: 两条历史在同一个拼写里相遇：一个日耳曼词表示一对，一个拉丁词表示灯芯；同族词反复回到配对、火与势均力敌。

normal.en: Old English gemæcca meant a mate or an equal, which is why match still names one half of a good pair.
normal.cn: 古英语 gemæcca 指配偶或地位相当的人，所以 match 至今指一对中的另一半。

normal.en: Latin myxa meant a lamp wick, and that wick sense came through Old French meiche into the English fire stick.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 myxa 指灯芯，这层意思经古法语 meiche 进入了英语的火柴义。

normal.en: Matchbox and matchmaker are compounds, and both keep the pairing or the fire in plain view.
normal.cn: matchbox 与 matchmaker 都是复合词，一个把火摆在明处，一个把配对摆在明处。

normal.en: Mismatch adds mis- for a bad pairing, while unmatched adds un- for having no equal.
normal.cn: mismatch 加 mis- 指配得不好，unmatched 加 un- 指没有对手。

normal.en: Match as a verb asks you to put two things side by side until they fit; nothing is compared in the abstract.
normal.cn: 作动词的 match 要求你把两样东西摆在一起，直到它们对得上；比较从不发生在空处。

abstract.en: Pairing and fire meet in one word because both happen in a single instant of contact.
abstract.cn: 配对与火在一个词里相遇，因为两者都发生在接触的一瞬。

abstract.en: A match is a test of fit: the right two things leave nothing to correct.
abstract.cn: match 是一场契合的检验：对的那两样东西，不留需要修改的地方。

abstract.en: From a lamp wick to a whistle, the word keeps finding two sides and making them face each other.
abstract.cn: 从灯芯到哨声，这个词一直在寻找两边，让它们面对面。

examples.en: The two teams will play a match on Saturday.
examples.cn: 两队将在星期六进行一场比赛。

examples.en: She struck a match to light the candle.
examples.cn: 她划着一根火柴点蜡烛。

examples.en: No one can match his speed on the track.
examples.cn: 跑道上没有人比得上他的速度。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马吃」——马要吃草，先得有人擦着一根小木梗点火；记住 match 是火柴，也是比赛和相配。

root: 这个词有两条来源：表示「一对、配偶」的义项出自古英语 gemæcca（配偶、地位相当的人）；表示「火柴」的义项出自拉丁语 myxa（灯芯），经希腊语与古法语 meiche 进入英语，两条词形后来合流。

sensesIntro.en: The core is two things brought face to face; the senses divide into the contest of two sides, the strike of a wick, the fitting partner, the act of fitting, and the equal who cannot be beaten.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是两样东西被摆到彼此对面；义项由此分成两方的比赛、灯芯的一划、合适的伴侣、使彼此契合的动作，以及无人能敌的对手。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin stick scrapes across a box and a spark jumps, while two teams stand face to face.
core.cn: 核心意象：细木划过盒面迸出火星，两队人也正好站到对面。

branches.en: a whistle at the centre of a packed stand
branches.cn: 满座看台中央的一声哨响

branches.en: a spark taken from a box in a dark room
branches.cn: 暗屋里从盒面擦出的一点火星

branches.en: two people pushed together and finding they fit
branches.cn: 两个人被推到一处，发现彼此合适

branches.en: curtains chosen to sit beside an old wall
branches.cn: 照着老墙颜色挑出的窗帘

branches.en: a runner pulling level with the one ahead
branches.cn: 跑者追平了前面那一个人

intro.en: An Old English noun for a pair, a Latin noun for a wick, their French and English descendants, and three English endings carry the two histories into one modern word.
intro.cn: 一个表示「一对」的古英语名词、一个表示「灯芯」的拉丁语名词、它们在法语与英语里的后代，再加三个英语词尾，把两条历史装进一个现代词。

latinIntro.en: Only the fire sense has a Latin line: myxa, the lamp wick, came through Greek and Old French. The pairing sense is Germanic and has no Latin cognate.
latinIntro.cn: 只有「火柴」这一义项有拉丁线索：myxa（灯芯）经希腊语与古法语传来；「配对」这一义项属日耳曼语，没有拉丁同族词。

definition_zh: 自然环境的；生态环境的；周围环境的；环境因素的；环境保护的；环境艺术的
definition_en: relating to the natural world and its condition; relating to a person's or organism's surroundings and conditions; concerned with protecting nature; (biology) arising from external conditions rather than genes; (art) concerned with the experience of a space
core_image: 一圈看不见的膜把人和周围的一切隔开又连上：你呼吸的空气、踩的地、听见的噪声都在这一圈里
scene: 工厂代表指着监测屏上的水质曲线。 The plant manager points at the water-quality curve and says the report assesses the environmental impact of the project.
sceneCN: 这里 environmental 是「环境的、环境影响的」（第 1 个义项：与自然环境及其状况相关）；句意：代表指着水质曲线说，这份报告评估项目的环境影响。图中可辨识物件：监测屏、水质曲线、取样瓶、工厂厂区。

pos.zh: 自然环境的；生态环境的；环境保护的（常与 impact / protection / law 连用）
周围环境的；由环境引起的；（艺术）环境艺术的（较专业用法）

derivatives.zh: 环境；周围状况
在环境方面；环保地
环境保护主义
环保主义者；环保的

senses.title: Relating to the natural world
senses.definition: relating to the natural world, especially its air, water, land, and living systems
senses.definitionCN: 与自然世界相关，尤指空气、水、土地与生命系统
senses.example: The project underwent a full environmental review before construction.
senses.exampleCN: 项目在施工前接受了全面的环境审查。
senses.why: Environmental is environment + -al. Environment is environ + -ment, where environ 'to surround' comes from Old French environ 'around'. The adjective therefore begins with the image of everything that surrounds a living thing.
senses.whyCN: environmental 是 environment + -al。environment 是 environ + -ment，其中 environ“包围”来自古法语 environ“在周围”。因此这个形容词的起点是“包围着生命体的一切”这一意象。

senses.title: Relating to surroundings or conditions
senses.definition: relating to the conditions, objects, and influences that surround a person, organism, or activity
senses.definitionCN: 与包围着人、生物或活动的条件、物体与影响相关
senses.example: Temperature and light are key environmental variables in the experiment.
senses.exampleCN: 温度与光照是实验中的关键环境变量。
senses.why: This is the broader, non-green sense: environment can be a laboratory room or a social setting. The adjective simply says 'of the surroundings', and context decides which surroundings count.
senses.whyCN: 这是更宽、非“环保”的义项：environment 可以是实验室房间或社会环境。形容词只说“周围状况的”，至于算哪些周围，由语境决定。

senses.title: Concerned with protecting nature
senses.definition: relating to efforts, laws, or groups that aim to protect nature from harm
senses.definitionCN: 与旨在保护自然免受损害的努力、法律或团体相关
senses.example: Environmental groups challenged the permit in court.
senses.exampleCN: 环保团体在法庭上质疑该许可。
senses.why: By metonymy the word shifts from 'of the environment' to 'protecting the environment'. This is the dominant everyday sense in news and policy, and it carries an implicit stance rather than a neutral description.
senses.whyCN: 通过转喻，这个词从“环境的”转到“保护环境的”。这是新闻与政策中最主要的日常义，它带有隐含立场，而非中性描述。

senses.title: Relating to environmental health
senses.definition: relating to conditions that affect public health, such as air quality, water safety, and waste
senses.definitionCN: 与影响公共卫生的状况相关，如空气质量、饮水安全与废物
senses.example: The agency investigates environmental health risks in old housing.
senses.exampleCN: 该机构调查老旧住房中的环境卫生风险。
senses.why: Public health uses the adjective to connect illness to place: lead paint, bad air, and contaminated water are environmental exposures. Here nature and human health are measured together.
senses.whyCN: 公共卫生用这个形容词把疾病与地点连起来：含铅涂料、劣质空气与受污染的水都是环境暴露。这里自然与人类健康被一起衡量。

senses.title: Arising from external conditions in biology
senses.titleCN: 生物学中由外部条件引起的
senses.definition: caused by external conditions rather than by genetic inheritance
senses.definitionCN: 由外部条件而非遗传引起
senses.example: The study separated genetic from environmental causes of the disease.
senses.exampleCN: 该研究把这种病的遗传成因与环境成因分开。
senses.why: Biology uses the term in the nature–nurture contrast: environmental effects are everything the genome does not supply. The adjective marks a cause, not a setting, which is why it pairs with 'factors' and 'influences'.
senses.whyCN: 生物学在“先天—后天”对照中使用这个术语：环境效应是基因组未提供的一切。这个形容词标记的是原因，而非场景，所以常与 factors、influences 搭配。

senses.title: Relating to environmental art
senses.definition: relating to art that treats a place, space, or landscape as part of the work
senses.definitionCN: 与把地点、空间或景观作为作品一部分的艺术相关
senses.example: The environmental installation changed how visitors moved through the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 这件环境装置改变了观众在大厅中移动的方式。
senses.why: Art criticism uses 'environmental' for works that surround the viewer rather than hang in front of them. This sense is unrelated to ecology; the shared word is 'surroundings'.
senses.whyCN: 艺术批评用 environmental 指包围观众、而非挂在观众面前的作品。这个义项与生态无关，共享的词义是“周围”。

senses.title: Subject to environmental regulation
senses.definition: governed by rules on pollution, land use, or ecological impact
senses.definitionCN: 受污染、土地使用或生态影响方面的规则约束
senses.example: The plant needs an environmental permit to discharge treated water.
senses.exampleCN: 该厂需要环境许可才能排放处理过的水。
senses.why: Legal usage nominalizes the word into fixed phrases: environmental law, environmental impact assessment, environmental permit. Here the adjective marks a regulatory domain with defined procedures.
senses.whyCN: 法律用法把这个词名物化为固定短语：environmental law、environmental impact assessment、environmental permit。这里形容词标记一个有既定程序的监管领域。

senses.title: Environmentally oriented in design
senses.definition: designed or operated with low harm to the environment in mind
senses.definitionCN: 在设计或运行上以低环境损害为取向
senses.example: The building's environmental features include grey-water reuse and passive cooling.
senses.exampleCN: 这栋建筑的环境友好特性包括中水回用与被动降温。
senses.why: Engineering extends the word to products and buildings: environmental design is design that accounts for resources and emissions. It overlaps with 'green' and 'sustainable' but is more technical and less promotional.
senses.whyCN: 工程学把词扩展到产品与建筑：environmental design 是考虑资源与排放的设计。它与 green、sustainable 重叠，但更技术化、更少宣传色彩。

intro.en: Environmental is environment + -al. Environment is a French-derived noun: environ 'to surround' + -ment. Environ comes from Old French environ 'around', built on viron 'circuit', whose further origin is uncertain. English environmental is a nineteenth-century adjective, and its 'green' sense is largely a twentieth-century development.
intro.cn: environmental 是 environment + -al。environment 是法语来源名词：environ“包围”+ -ment。environ 来自古法语 environ“在周围”，建立在 viron“环、圈”上，更早来源不确定。英语 environmental 是 19 世纪形容词，其“环保”义主要是 20 世纪的发展。

items.en: Old French environ meant 'around, in a circle', from en- 'in' plus viron 'circuit, circle'. The verb environner 'to surround' and the noun environnement developed from it.
items.cn: 古法语 environ 意为“在周围、成圈”，由 en-“在内”加 viron“环、圈”构成。动词 environner“包围”与名词 environnement 由此发展。

items.en: The origin of viron 'circle' is uncertain. It may be linked to virer 'to turn', but the further etymology of virer is itself disputed; no reliable Latin source can be asserted.
items.cn: viron“环、圈”的来源不确定。它可能与 virer“转动”有关，但 virer 的更早词源本身有争议；无法断言可靠的拉丁来源。

items.en: English borrowed environment in the seventeenth century as 'the act of surrounding' and 'surrounding conditions'. The modern sense of natural surroundings consolidated in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries.
items.cn: 英语于 17 世纪借入 environment，义为“包围的行为”与“周围状况”。自然环境的现代义在 18、19 世纪逐步定型。

items.en: Environmental appears as the adjective of environment in the nineteenth century. Early uses concern surroundings and conditions generally, not pollution or ecology.
items.cn: environmental 于 19 世纪作为 environment 的形容词出现。早期用法泛指周围与条件，而非污染或生态。

items.en: With the rise of ecology and the environmental movement after the mid-twentieth century, the adjective shifted toward nature protection: environmental law, environmental impact, environmental groups.
items.cn: 20 世纪中叶以后，随着生态学与环保运动的兴起，这个形容词转向自然保护：environmental law、environmental impact、environmental groups。

items.en: The word now spans laboratory variables, public health, art installations, and building design. The unifying idea is still 'what surrounds', which is why one adjective can serve ecology and aesthetics at once.
items.cn: 这个词如今覆盖实验室变量、公共卫生、艺术装置与建筑设计。统一的概念仍是“包围着什么”，所以一个形容词能同时服务生态与美学。

note.en: The first group separates the environment family from look-alikes; the second group separates environmental from neighbouring adjectives of nature and surroundings.
note.cn: 第一组区分 environment 词族与形近词；第二组区分 environmental 与相邻的“自然”“周围”形容词。

entries.definition: the surroundings or conditions in which something exists. It is the noun that -al turns into the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 某物存在的周围状况或条件。它是被 -al 转化为形容词的名词。

entries.definition: in a way that relates to or affects the environment, as in environmentally friendly. It modifies an adjective or verb, not a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 以与环境相关或影响环境的方式，如 environmentally friendly。它修饰形容词或动词，而非名词。

entries.definition: to surround or encircle. It is the oldest member of the family and now rare outside 'environment'.
entries.definitionCN: 包围、环绕。它是词族中最古老的成员，如今除 environment 外很少见。

entries.definition: relating to ecology, the study of organisms and their interactions. It is more technical than environmental and not necessarily about protection.
entries.definitionCN: 与生态学相关，即研究生物及其互动。它比 environmental 更技术化，也不一定涉及保护。

entries.definition: existing or happening around something. It is neutral and spatial, while environmental can imply conditions or regulation.
entries.definitionCN: 存在于或发生在某物周围的。它中性且空间化，而 environmental 可暗示条件或法规。

entries.definition: environmentally friendly, often used in marketing. It is looser and more promotional than environmental.
entries.definitionCN: 环保的，常用于营销。它比 environmental 更松、更带宣传色彩。

normalIntro.en: Real associations: environ 'to surround', the -ment noun, the -al adjective, and fixed phrases such as environmental impact and environmental law.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联想：environ“包围”、-ment 名词、-al 形容词，以及 environmental impact、environmental law 等固定短语。

normal.en: environ means 'to surround': environment is everything that surrounds us, and -al makes it the adjective.
normal.cn: environ 意为“包围”：environment 是包围我们的一切，-al 使它成为形容词。

normal.en: environment + -al: keep the -ment and add -al; the adverb then adds -ly.
normal.cn: environment + -al：保留 -ment 再加 -al；副词再加 -ly。

normal.en: Environmental impact, environmental law, environmental protection: the three phrases cover most news uses.
normal.cn: environmental impact、environmental law、environmental protection：这三个短语覆盖了大部分新闻用法。

normal.en: In biology, environmental means 'caused from outside', the opposite of genetic.
normal.cn: 生物学中 environmental 意为“由外部引起的”，与 genetic 相对。

normal.en: Environmental art surrounds the viewer; it borrows the word's oldest sense of 'surroundings', not its green sense.
normal.cn: 环境艺术包围观众；它借的是这个词最古老的“周围”义，而非环保义。

abstract.en: An environment is not a backdrop but a set of conditions that enter the body with every breath.
abstract.cn: 环境不是背景板，而是一套随每次呼吸进入身体的条件。

abstract.en: To call something environmental is to admit that its causes and effects cross its own boundary.
abstract.cn: 把某事称为 environmental，就是承认它的因果越过了自身边界。

abstract.en: Protection and surroundings share one word because what surrounds us is also what we must defend.
abstract.cn: 保护与周围共享一个词，因为包围我们的事物也是我们必须守护的事物。

examples.en: The environmental impact of the dam was assessed over three years.
examples.cn: 大坝的环境影响经过三年评估。

examples.en: Environmental factors explain part of the difference in height between the groups.
examples.cn: 环境因素解释了各组身高差异的一部分。

examples.en: The city adopted stricter environmental rules on waste water.
examples.cn: 该市对废水采取了更严格的环境规定。

dict_mnemonic.text: “因外绕，门头”——因为外面绕着一圈东西，门口就成了环境 → environmental 环境的

root: environ（包围，古法语 environ“在周围”）+ -ment（名词后缀）+ -al（形容词后缀）；字面义“包围着（我们）的”，核心是“与周围状况或自然世界相关”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of environmental spread outward from one idea: what surrounds a thing. That surrounding can be nature, a laboratory, a body, a genome's absence, a gallery space, a legal regime, or a building's design. The 'green' sense is the most visible today but not the oldest.
sensesIntro.cn: environmental 的八个义项都从一个观念向外展开：包围某物的一切。这个“周围”可以是自然、实验室、身体、基因之外的因素、画廊空间、法律体制或建筑设计。“环保”义今天最显眼，却不是最古老的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an invisible membrane that both separates a living thing from its surroundings and connects it to them.
core.cn: 核心意象：一层看不见的膜，既把生命体与周围隔开，又把它与周围连在一起。

branches.en: WHAT SURROUNDS: the natural world and the laboratory's variables are both the set of conditions around a thing.
branches.cn: 包围之物：自然世界与实验室变量都是某物周围的条件集合。

branches.en: PROTECTION AND HEALTH: the adjective turns from describing surroundings to defending them, and to health effects that enter through them.
branches.cn: 保护与健康：形容词从描述周围转为守护周围，并指向通过周围进入健康的影响。

branches.en: CAUSE: in biology, environmental marks what the genome does not supply.
branches.cn: 原因：生物学中 environmental 标记基因组未提供的东西。

branches.en: ART: the work surrounds the viewer, using the oldest sense of the word.
branches.cn: 艺术：作品包围观众，用的是这个词最古老的义。

branches.en: REGULATION AND DESIGN: law defines the domain, and engineering builds products that lower their load on it.
branches.cn: 法规与设计：法律界定领域，工程建造降低环境负荷的产品。

intro.en: Environmental is a two-suffix adjective: environ + -ment + -al. The affix set shows the noun, adverb, and related forms, and warns that the root viron is of uncertain origin.
intro.cn: environmental 是双后缀形容词：environ + -ment + -al。词缀组展示名词、副词与相关形式，并提醒词根 viron 来源不确定。

latinIntro.en: Old French viron 'circle' and environ 'around' yield the verb environner and the noun environnement; English adds -al. No reliable Latin cognate for viron can be asserted, so the Latin entries are left empty rather than invented.
latinIntro.cn: 古法语 viron“圈”与 environ“在周围”产生动词 environner 与名词 environnement；英语再加 -al。无法断言 viron 有可靠拉丁同源词，因此拉丁条目留空，而不编造。

items.meaning: relating to surroundings or the natural world
items.meaningCN: 环境的；环保的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: The environmental review took a year.

items.meaning: the conditions or surroundings of something

items.meaningCN: 在环境方面；环保地（-ly 构成副词）

items.meaning: a movement to protect the natural world
items.meaningCN: 环境保护主义（-ism 表主义）
items.exampleCN: 环保主义在 1970 年代迅速发展。

items.meaning: a person who works to protect nature
items.exampleCN: 环保主义者反对这条新路。
树木环绕着这座老房子。

items.meaning: the effect of an activity on the surroundings
items.example: The environmental impact was rated low.

items.meaning: the body of rules protecting the natural world

definition_zh: 百；一百；数百；许多
definition_en: the number 100, or a very large number of things
core_image: 数到尽头的一整排一百个格子
scene: 操场上队伍很长。 There were three hundred students at the sports meeting.
sceneCN: 这里 hundred 是「百」（第 1 个义项：数词一百）；句意：运动会上有三百名学生。

derivatives.zh: 第一百；由基数加序数后缀构成
英担（重量单位）；复合词

senses.title: The number 100
senses.definition: the cardinal number 100
senses.definitionCN: 基数词一百
senses.example: The hall holds six hundred people.
senses.exampleCN: 礼堂能容纳六百人。
senses.why: The word names the base counting unit; with a numeral before it, it does not take a plural s.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名基本计数单位，前面有数字时不加复数 s。

senses.title: Hundreds of: a large indefinite number
senses.definition: a very large but uncounted number of things
senses.definitionCN: 数量很大但未清点的事物
senses.example: Hundreds of birds flew over the lake.
senses.exampleCN: 数百只鸟飞过湖面。
senses.why: Take the round number and stretch it beyond exact counting: it becomes a vague marker of many.
senses.whyCN: 把整数延伸到清点之外，就变成表示「多」的模糊标记。

senses.title: A division of counting or age
senses.definition: a section of a number scale, or a century of age
senses.definitionCN: 数位上的百位，或以百年计的时段
senses.example: She is in her hundredth year.
senses.exampleCN: 她已年过九十九。
senses.why: The unit also slices scales: place value, years, or ordered positions like the hundredth.
senses.whyCN: 这个单位也用来切分刻度：数位、年份或第一百这样的序位。

senses.title: A perfect score or total
senses.definition: a complete score out of a hundred, or total agreement
senses.definitionCN: 百分制中的满分，或完全一致
senses.example: He gave the plan a hundred percent support.
senses.exampleCN: 他对这个计划百分之百支持。
senses.why: Because a hundred is the whole of a standard scale, it stands for completeness.
senses.whyCN: 一百是标准刻度的全部，所以可以代表完整、全部。

intro.en: Hundred comes from Old English hund, hundred, combined with -red, a count or reckoning. Germanic peoples counted by long hundreds of one hundred and twenty, and the word also named an old administrative district.
intro.cn: hundred 来自古英语 hund「百」加 -red「计数」。日耳曼人的「长百」为一百二十，该词也曾指古代的行政区。

items.en: The reconstructed form combines hund, ten, with a root redh, to count, giving the sense a count of ten decades.
items.cn: 重构形式由 hund「十」加 redh「计数」词根构成，意为「十个十的计数」。

items.en: Old English hundred meant both the number and a district of one hundred households used for taxes and courts.
items.cn: 古英语 hundred 既指数词，也指用于征税与司法的百户行政区。

items.en: Old Norse hundrað sometimes counted one hundred and twenty, the long hundred of northern trade.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 hundrað 有时指一百二十，即北方贸易中的「长百」。

items.en: Middle English kept both the counting and the district senses; the administrative sense later faded except in place names.
items.cn: 中古英语保留了计数与行政区两义，后者后来只残留在地名中。

items.en: Modern English settled on the plain number, adding the vague hundreds of and the perfect-score sense.
items.cn: 现代英语固定为单纯数词，并发展出 hundreds of 的模糊义与满分义。

note.en: The look-alike group lists related number words. The meaning group gathers other vague large-quantity markers.
note.cn: 形近组列出相关数词；词义组收集其他表示大量事物的模糊说法。

entries.definition: position 100 in a series, or one part of a hundred.
entries.definitionCN: 第一百；百分之一。由本词加序数后缀构成。

entries.definition: an old unit of weight, about fifty kilograms in Britain.
entries.definitionCN: 英担。旧重量单位，英国约合五十公斤。

entries.definition: a person who hunts. Only the letters look similar; the root is hunt.
entries.definitionCN: 猎人。只是字形相近，词根是 hunt。

entries.definition: twelve of something, or dozens of for an indefinite many.
entries.definitionCN: 一打；dozens of 表示大量。

entries.definition: the number 1,000; thousands of marks an even bigger crowd.
entries.definitionCN: 千；thousands of 表示更大量。

entries.definition: an extremely large number, originally ten thousand in Greek.
entries.definitionCN: 无数。希腊语原指一万，今为书面语的大量。

normalIntro.en: These hooks anchor hundred in counting by tens and in the family of hundredth and hundreds of.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩把 hundred 锚定在十进制计数和 hundredth、hundreds of 词族上。

normal.en: Count ten tens: ten, twenty ... one hundred. Hundred is ten tens.
normal.cn: 十个十相加：十、二十……一百。hundred 就是十个十。

normal.en: With a number in front, no s: three hundred; alone or vague, add s: hundreds of.
normal.cn: 前面有数字不加 s：three hundred；泛指则加 s：hundreds of。

normal.en: hundredth shifts it to order or fraction: the hundredth day, one hundredth of the cost.
normal.cn: hundredth 把它变成序数或分数：第一百天、百分之一的成本。

normal.en: Old law counted people: a hundred was a district of one hundred households.
normal.cn: 古法按人计数：hundred 曾是百户行政区。

normal.en: a hundred percent means everything, not just the number on a test.
normal.cn: a hundred percent 指全部投入，不只是卷面分数。

abstract.en: One image: a full grid of one hundred little squares, every cell filled.
abstract.cn: 只记一个画面：一百个小格子组成的大格子，每格都填满。

abstract.en: Feel the jump: ten is hands, hundred is beyond two hands, a crowd.
abstract.cn: 感受跳跃：十是双手，百超出双手，成群。

abstract.en: Treat hundred as a fence post on the number line where vague many begins.
abstract.cn: 把 hundred 当数轴上「模糊的多」开始的界桩。

examples.en: The library holds hundreds of old maps.
examples.cn: 图书馆藏有数百幅古地图。

examples.en: She ran the hundred meters in twelve seconds.
examples.cn: 她十二秒跑完一百米。

examples.en: Over two hundred guests attended the wedding.
examples.cn: 两百多位客人参加了婚礼。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「汗的瑞的」：数到一百，汗都数出来了，何其多。

root: 古英语 hund「百」+ -red「计数」（日耳曼语词根），与德语 Hundert 同源；古诺斯语 hundrað 曾计一百二十，古英语中亦指百户行政区。

sensesIntro.en: Hundred begins as the exact number, then loosens into vague plenty, slices scales into order and fraction, and finally stands for the whole of a standard score.
sensesIntro.cn: hundred 从精确的数起步，松弛为泛指的大量，把刻度切成序位与分数，最终代表标准分里的全部。

core.en: A full round unit of counting, beyond which exact counting turns into vague many.
core.cn: 一个完整的整数单位，越过它精确计数就变成模糊的多。

branches.en: EXACT NUMBER: the cardinal 100, unchanged after numerals.
branches.cn: 精确数词：基数一百，跟在数字后不变。

branches.en: VAGUE MANY: hundreds of things you never bother to count.
branches.cn: 泛指大量：hundreds of，多到懒得清点。

branches.en: SCALE POSITION: place value, centuries of life, the hundredth in a series.
branches.cn: 刻度位置：数位、百年人生、系列中的第一百。

branches.en: TOTAL SCORE: a hundred percent of effort or support.
branches.cn: 满分：百分之百的努力或支持。

branches.en: ADMINISTRATION: the old hundred as a district built on a count of households.
branches.cn: 行政区：旧时以百户计数划分的 hundred 区。

intro.en: Hundred forms few derivatives, but the ordinal hundredth and the compound hundredweight are regular family members.
intro.cn: hundred 派生不多，序数词 hundredth 与复合词 hundredweight 是常规词族成员。

latinIntro.en: This family is Germanic, so the Latin entries section stays empty; the related numbers come from the same Germanic counting system.
latinIntro.cn: 本词族属日耳曼源，拉丁同源词一栏留空；相关数词出自同一日耳曼计数系统。

items.example: A hundred steps lead to the tower.

items.meaning: number 100 in a series; one of 100 equal parts
items.example: This is the hundredth copy printed.
Hundreds of boats fill the harbor.
The sacks were sold by the hundredweight.

items.meaningCN: 一百零一；也指琐碎细节
items.example: She gave a hundred and one excuses.
items.exampleCN: 她找了一百零一个借口。
比率千分之五十地上升了。

items.example: Traders once reckoned a long hundred of hides.
items.exampleCN: 商人旧时按长百计皮货。

definition_zh: 毕业生；毕业；把……分刻度；研究生的
definition_en: a person who has completed a degree, or to complete one and move up to the next stage
core_image: 一位穿毕业袍的人把证书夹在臂下，另一只手提着一只标有刻度线的量筒
scene: 实验室里，新来的助理先量出准确体积，再把量筒放回架上。 She graduated from the programme and now works in the same lab.
sceneCN: 新助理量出准确体积后把量筒放回架上，她刚从该项目毕业并留在这间实验室；句中的 graduate 指「完成学业取得学位」（第 2 个义项：读完课程并获授学位）。图中可辨识物件：毕业袍、证书、量筒刻度、实验台。

逐渐的
