senses.title: A person who holds a degree
senses.definition: someone who has completed a degree or a course of study
senses.definitionCN: 已完成学位或一段学业的人
senses.example: The firm hires two graduates each spring.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司每年春天招聘两名毕业生。
senses.why: the Latin past participle graduatus named someone advanced step by step, and English kept it as the word for the finished student.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁过去分词 graduatus 指逐级晋升的人，英语把它保留为「学业已完成者」的称呼。

senses.title: To complete a degree
senses.definition: to finish a course of study and be formally awarded a degree
senses.definitionCN: 读完一段学业并被正式授予学位
senses.example: She graduated from the programme and now works in the same lab.
senses.exampleCN: 她从该项目毕业，如今在同一间实验室工作。
senses.why: the verb began as 'to take a degree' in Medieval Latin, so it names the moment of formal completion.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词在中世纪拉丁语中本为「取得学位」，因此它命名的正是正式完成的那一刻。

senses.title: To move up a level
senses.definition: to move from one stage or rank to a higher one
senses.definitionCN: 从一个阶段或等级升到更高的一级
senses.example: The junior clerk graduated to head of section in four years.
senses.exampleCN: 这位低级职员四年内升到科长。
senses.why: the step image survives outside school: any promotion or transfer upward can be called a graduation.
senses.whyCN: 台阶意象在校外仍然存活：任何向上晋升或转入更高位置都可称为 graduate。

senses.title: Postgraduate, as an adjective
senses.definition: describing study or a school that comes after a first degree
senses.definitionCN: 描述取得首个学位之后的学业或院校
senses.example: He moved into graduate study after two years of teaching.
senses.exampleCN: 教了两年书之后，他转入研究生学习。
senses.why: American usage fixed the adjective to the stage above the bachelor's degree, which is why graduate school names a place, not a person.
senses.whyCN: 美式用法把这个形容词固定在学士之上的阶段，因此「研究生院」这类说法指的是一个地方而非一个人。

senses.title: To mark a scale in degrees
senses.definition: to divide a vessel or instrument into regular measured marks
senses.definitionCN: 把容器或仪器分成规则的测量刻线
senses.example: The glass was graduated in millilitres on one side.
senses.exampleCN: 这只玻璃器皿一侧按毫升划了刻度。
senses.why: the oldest technical sense is physical: to graduate a vessel is to give it steps that can be read.
senses.whyCN: 最早的技术义是物理性的：给容器「分度」就是给它可读的台阶。

senses.title: A secondary-school finisher
senses.definition: in American usage, a person who has finished high school
senses.definitionCN: 在美式用法中，指读完高中的人
senses.example: Half the town turned out for the high school graduates.
senses.exampleCN: 半个镇子的人都出来为高中毕业生庆祝。
senses.why: American speech widened the noun downward to secondary school, so the word no longer guarantees a degree.
senses.whyCN: 美式口语把名词向下扩展到中学，因此这个词不再保证持有学位。

senses.title: To pass through stages
senses.definition: to change by small steps from one condition to another
senses.definitionCN: 以一种状态按小步转入另一种状态
senses.example: The colours graduate from pale yellow to deep orange.
senses.exampleCN: 色彩从浅黄逐步过渡到深橙。
senses.why: the step sense turns abstract again here: a continuous change is read as a series of degrees.
senses.whyCN: 台阶义在此再次抽象化：连续的变化被读成一串度数。

senses.title: A trained programme finisher
senses.titleCN: 完成培训项目的结业者
senses.definition: a person who has completed a specified training programme, as in nursing
senses.definitionCN: 完成某项特定培训项目的人，如护理专业
senses.example: The ward employs two nurse graduates from the new cohort.
senses.exampleCN: 该病区雇用了新一批护理专业的结业者。
senses.why: training programmes use the noun for anyone who has finished their course, whether or not a degree is awarded.
senses.whyCN: 培训项目用这个名词指任何完成课程的人，无论是否授予学位。

intro.en: Graduate comes from Latin graduatus, the past participle of graduari 'to take a degree', from gradus 'step'. The noun and the marking verb entered English by different routes in the fifteenth and seventeenth centuries. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: graduate 来自拉丁 graduatus，即 graduari「取得学位」的过去分词，源于 gradus「台阶」。名词与「划刻度」的动词用法在十五与十七世纪经不同路径进入英语。年代为约数。

items.en: Gradus meant 'step, stride, degree', the shared source of the stair and the scale.
items.cn: gradus 意为「台阶、步伐、度数」，是楼梯与量具的共同来源。

items.en: Graduari meant 'to take a degree, to be advanced step by step'. It described the student who had climbed all the required steps.
items.cn: graduari 意为「取得学位、逐级晋升」，描述已爬完所有必需台阶的学生。

items.en: The past participle graduatus named the person who had been advanced, and it is the direct source of the English noun.
items.cn: 过去分词 graduatus 指已被晋升的人，是英语名词的直接来源。

items.en: English graduate appeared in the fifteenth century for a person holding a degree, and the university sense dominated for centuries.
items.cn: 英语 graduate 于十五世纪出现，指持有学位的人，此后数百年间以大学义为主。

items.en: In the seventeenth century the same form was used as a verb for dividing a vessel into degrees, which is why a graduated cylinder carries the word without any school.
items.cn: 十七世纪，同一词形被用作动词，指把容器分成度数，因此在「刻度量筒」这样的说法里，这个词与学校毫无关系。

items.en: The deeper origin of gradus and gradi is uncertain; the link to a root meaning 'to step, go' is a reconstruction. The American widening of the noun to secondary school is recent and only loosely documented.
items.cn: gradus 与 gradi 的更早来源不确定；与表示「迈步、行走」的词根的联系属重构形式。名词在美式用法中向中学扩展是晚近现象，记录亦不严密。

note.en: Group one holds the step-root family, including the two words most often confused with this one; group two holds the people and stages around finishing study.
note.cn: 第一组是「台阶」词根词族，包括最易与它混淆的两个词；第二组是围绕完成学业的人与阶段。

entries.definition: The act, the ceremony or the scale marks; graduate is the person or the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指行为、仪式或刻度；graduate 指人或动词。

entries.definition: Changing little by little; it describes pace, not the completion of study.
entries.definitionCN: 指一点一点变化，描述节奏而非完成学业。

entries.definition: The institution for study after a first degree; the adjective sense lives mainly in this and similar compounds.
entries.definitionCN: 指取得首个学位后就读的院校；形容词义主要活在此类复合词中。

entries.definition: A student who has not yet taken a first degree, the rung below the graduate.
entries.definitionCN: 指尚未取得首个学位的学生，是 graduate 下面的一级。

entries.definition: A former student of a particular school, whether or not recently graduated; it stresses loyalty to the institution.
entries.definitionCN: 指某校的旧生，无论是否刚毕业；强调对院校的归属。

entries.definition: British usage for study after a bachelor's degree, close to the adjective sense of graduate.
entries.definitionCN: 英式说法，指学士之后的学业，接近 graduate 的形容词义。

entries.definition: A British term for someone finishing secondary school, with no implication of a degree.
entries.definitionCN: 英式说法，指读完中学的人，不含学位之意。

entries.definition: The holder of a first degree, a specific rank rather than a general finisher.
entries.definitionCN: 指首个学位的持有者，是具体等级而非泛称的完成者。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations here are the real step root, the real double life of the word in schools and laboratories, and the real American usage.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想取自真实的台阶词根、这个词在学校与实验室之间的真实双重身份，以及真实的美式用法。

normal.en: gradus 'step': a graduate has reached the top of the stair.
normal.cn: gradus「台阶」：graduate 已走到楼梯顶端。

normal.en: Graduari 'to take a degree' gave the noun; to graduate a vessel gave the measuring verb.
normal.cn: graduari「取得学位」给出名词；给容器分度则给出测量的动词义。

normal.en: The family runs graduation, gradual, gradually, undergraduate, postgraduate.
normal.cn: 词族包括 graduation、gradual、gradually、undergraduate、postgraduate。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the school sense: graduate from, graduate school, graduate student.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出学校义：从……毕业、研究生院、研究生。

normal.en: The laboratory keeps the measuring sense: a graduated cylinder is read at the eye line.
normal.cn: 实验室保留测量义：量筒的读数要与视线齐平。

abstract.en: Picture a cap thrown into the air above a crowd of identical gowns.
abstract.cn: 想象一顶帽子被抛到一片相同毕业袍的上方。

abstract.en: Picture a glass tube ruled with fine lines, standing beside a diploma on the same bench.
abstract.cn: 想象一根划着细线的玻璃管，与一张文凭并排放在同一张台上。

abstract.en: Picture a staircase that continues past the stage and out of the building.
abstract.cn: 想象一座楼梯越过舞台，继续延伸到楼外。

examples.en: She graduated from a small college in the north.
examples.cn: 她从北方一所小学院毕业。

examples.en: The scheme hires recent graduates for two-year placements.
examples.cn: 该计划雇用应届毕业生做两年岗位实习。

examples.en: Every vessel in the cabinet is graduated in millilitres.
examples.cn: 柜中每件器皿都按毫升划了刻度。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「grad（台阶）」——走完台阶的人毕业，给量具刻上台阶就是分度 → 毕业生、毕业、分刻度

root: 拉丁 gradus「台阶、度数」（源自 gradi「迈步」）→ graduari「取得学位」→ 过去分词 graduatus → 英语 graduate；十七世纪同一词形又用作「给量具分度」。gradus 与 gradi 的更早来源不确定，与「迈步」词根的联系属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses climb one stair and then leave the school: a person reaches the top, the reaching becomes a verb, an upward move, a postgraduate adjective, a scale on a glass vessel, a high-school finisher, a gradual change and a trained programme finisher.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项先爬同一座楼梯，再走出校门：有人走到顶端，到达成为动词、向上的晋升、研究生的形容词、玻璃器皿上的刻度、中学结业者、渐变，以及完成培训项目的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a staircase that continues past the stage and out of the building, while a ruled glass tube stands on the same bench as a diploma.
core.cn: 核心意象：一座越过舞台、延伸出楼外的楼梯，而一根划着刻度的玻璃管与文凭并排放在同一张台上。

branches.en: THE PERSON AND THE ACT: the one at the top and the moment of arriving share one form.
branches.cn: 人与动作：站在顶端的人与到达的那一刻共用同一词形。

branches.en: THE NEXT STAGE: an upward move at work, and the adjective for study above a first degree.
branches.cn: 下一阶段：职场上的向上晋升，以及首个学位之后学业的形容词。

branches.en: THE RULED LINE: a vessel is divided into degrees, and continuous change is read as degrees too.
branches.cn: 刻线：器皿被分成度数，连续变化也被读成度数。

branches.en: THE WIDER NOUN: American speech lowers the word to secondary school, so a degree is no longer guaranteed.
branches.cn: 更宽的名词：美式口语把词降到中学，学位不再是保证。

branches.en: THE COURSE: any training programme can produce a graduate, degree or not.
branches.cn: 课程：任何培训项目都能产出结业者，有没有学位都一样。

intro.en: The word is a Latin root and participle ending, and the same pieces build the school family and the measuring words.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁词根与分词词尾构成，同一批部件造出学校词族与测量类词。

latinIntro.en: Gradus and gradi supply the step; graduari and its participle graduatus supply the person and the verb, while the same form was reused for marking a scale.
latinIntro.cn: gradus 与 gradi 提供「台阶」；graduari 及其分词 graduatus 提供人与动词，而同一词形又被用于划刻度。

items.example: Gradi is the verb behind the noun.
items.exampleCN: gradi 是名词背后的动词。

items.example: Graduatus is the direct source of the noun.
items.exampleCN: graduatus 是名词的直接来源。

items.meaning: a degree holder; to finish a degree
items.example: The noun and verb share one spelling.
items.exampleCN: 名词与动词共用一种拼写。

items.example: A graduated cylinder is read at eye level.
items.exampleCN: 量筒读数要与视线齐平。

items.meaning: a student below the first degree
items.meaningCN: 尚未取得首个学位的学生

derivatives.zh: 毕业；毕业典礼；刻度
逐渐的
逐渐地
本科生
研究生；研究生的

definition_zh: 浪费；废物、垃圾；浪费的时间或金钱；动词：浪费、滥用；荒废的
definition_en: to use something carelessly so that it is lost, or material that is thrown away because it is no longer wanted
core_image: 水从没关紧的龙头里一直滴，地上积成一片没人要的湿痕
scene: 食堂收餐口的桶里堆着大半个没吃完的饭盒。 So much food is wasted every day that the kitchen began weighing it.
sceneCN: 这里 waste 是「浪费」（第 4 个义项：不加珍惜地用掉，使之白白失去）；句意为每天浪费的食物太多，厨房开始称重。水白白流走、饭被倒掉，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 名词：废物、垃圾；浪费；荒地

derivatives.zh: 加后缀 -ful 构成，义为「浪费的；不节俭的」
加后缀 -age 构成，义为「损耗；浪费量」
加后缀 -er 构成，义为「浪费者；废品」
由过去分词转形容词，义为「被浪费的；憔悴的」

senses.title: A desert or empty land
senses.titleCN: 荒地：无人居住的空旷之地
senses.definition: a large area of land that is empty, wild and not used for farming
senses.definitionCN: 大片空旷、野生、不用于耕种的土地
senses.example: Beyond the last field lies a wide waste of stone and thorn.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一块田之外，是一片石头与荆棘的荒地。
senses.why: Old French wast meant empty and desolate, and English kept that picture of land with nothing on it.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 wast 意为「空的、荒凉的」，英语保留了那片空无一物的土地的画面。

senses.title: To destroy and leave empty
senses.titleCN: 使荒芜：毁坏而使之空无
senses.definition: to damage a place so badly that it is left empty or ruined
senses.definitionCN: 把某地毁坏到空无或残破的地步
senses.example: The long war wasted the whole valley.
senses.exampleCN: 漫长的战争让整个山谷变得荒芜。
senses.why: The adjective of emptiness becomes an action: to make a place into a waste.
senses.whyCN: 表示「空」的形容词变成动作：把某地变成一片荒地。

senses.title: Rubbish and unwanted material
senses.titleCN: 废物、垃圾：不再需要而被丢弃的东西
senses.definition: material that is no longer wanted and is thrown away
senses.definitionCN: 已不需要、被丢弃的物质
senses.example: The factory must treat its waste before it enters the river.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂必须先把废物处理掉，才能排入河中。
senses.why: What is left after use is like a wasteland: nothing grows on it, so it is set aside.
senses.whyCN: 用剩下的东西就像荒地：上面长不出什么，只好被弃置一旁。

senses.title: To use carelessly
senses.definition: to use money, time or effort badly, so that it brings no benefit
senses.definitionCN: 不善加利用金钱、时间或精力，使之无所收益
senses.example: Do not waste hot water on a small load of dishes.
senses.exampleCN: 别为几个碗浪费热水。
senses.why: Spending what could have been used well turns a resource into waste; the verb names that turning.
senses.whyCN: 把本可好好利用的东西花掉，资源就变成了废物；动词命名的正是这一转变。

senses.title: As in wasted effort or a wasted chance
senses.titleCN: 白白错过：努力或机会被耗掉
senses.definition: used of effort, opportunity or a person's condition when something valuable comes to nothing
senses.definitionCN: 用于努力、机会或人的状态，指宝贵的东西最终落空
senses.example: All their careful planning was wasted when the road was closed.
senses.exampleCN: 路一封闭，他们所有的精心安排都白费了。
senses.why: The lost value is no longer money but possibility: what might have happened now cannot.
senses.whyCN: 失去的不再是钱，而是可能性：本可能发生的事如今不可能了。

intro.en: Waste came from Latin vastus through Old French, and its first meaning was empty land.
intro.cn: waste 经古法语来自拉丁语 vastus，最初的意思是空旷的土地。

items.en: Vastus meant 'empty, desolate, huge'; the emptiness came before the size in English use.
items.cn: vastus 意为「空的、荒凉的、巨大的」；在英语用法中，空义先于大义。

items.en: The verb vastare meant 'to lay waste, to devastate', turning emptiness into an action.
items.cn: 动词 vastare 意为「使荒芜、毁坏」，把「空」变成了动作。

items.en: Old French had both gast and waste, meaning 'empty, ruined' and 'a waste place'.
items.cn: 古法语有 gast 与 waste 两种形式，意为「空的、毁坏的」与「荒地」。

items.en: English took waste as noun, adjective and verb together in the thirteenth century.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪同时把 waste 用作名词、形容词和动词。

items.en: Industry added the rubbish sense: household waste, waste paper, waste water.
items.cn: 工业补充了垃圾义：生活垃圾、废纸、废水。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words of the same empty-root family; the near-meaning group gathers ways of squandering and of rubbish.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「空」词根词族；近义组收挥霍与垃圾类说法。

entries.definition: Extremely large; the same Latin vastus, with the size sense only.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「辽阔的」，同出拉丁语 vastus，只保留「大」义。

entries.definition: To destroy a place completely; Latin de- plus vastare.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「毁坏」，由 de- 加 vastare 构成。

entries.definition: Using more than is needed; the adjective of the squandering sense.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「浪费的」，是挥霍义的形容词形式。

entries.definition: Land that is empty and cannot be farmed.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「荒地」，即空旷无法耕种之地。

entries.definition: To spend money or time foolishly; stronger and more disapproving.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「挥霍」，语气更强、更带责备。

entries.definition: Unwanted things; the British everyday word for waste.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「垃圾」，是英式日常说法。

entries.definition: Waste food and household rubbish; the American everyday word.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「垃圾」，尤指厨余，是美式日常说法。

entries.definition: To give or use without harming oneself; the opposite of wasting.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「腾出、剩下」，与浪费相对。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin vastus and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁语 vastus，以及这个词实际出现的短语。

normal.en: waste and vast share a root: empty land, and land just very big.
normal.cn: waste 与 vast 同根：一片是空地，一片只是很大。

normal.en: To waste is to turn a resource into rubbish.
normal.cn: waste 就是把资源变成垃圾。

normal.en: A waste of time costs more than a waste of paper.
normal.cn: 浪费时间的代价比浪费纸张大得多。

normal.en: Household waste is what leaves the house to be thrown away.
normal.cn: household waste 就是被运出家门的垃圾。

normal.en: Lay waste to a place and it becomes a waste: the verb and the noun meet.
normal.cn: lay waste to 一个地方，它就变成一片 waste：动词与名词在此相遇。

abstract.en: Picture a tap left dripping overnight: the water is not dirty, only lost.
abstract.cn: 想象一只水龙头一夜没关紧：水并不脏，只是白白流掉了。

abstract.en: The two halves of the word meet at the same point: what is thrown away is what was never used well.
abstract.cn: 这个词的两半在同一点相遇：被丢弃的，正是从未被好好利用的。

abstract.en: Emptiness is the hinge: a wasted field, a wasted chance and a waste bin all hold nothing useful.
abstract.cn: 空是那个铰链：荒掉的地、白费的机会、垃圾箱，都装着没用的东西。

examples.en: He wasted two hours waiting for a bus that never came.
examples.cn: 他白等了两个小时，那趟公交始终没来。

examples.en: The city collects household waste every Tuesday.
examples.cn: 这座城市每周二收集生活垃圾。

examples.en: It is a waste of money to buy a new one when this still works.
examples.cn: 这个还能用，再买个新的纯属浪费钱。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喂（wei）死它（ste）」——把好东西喂给垃圾桶，活活浪费：浪费

root: 源自拉丁语 vastus「空的、荒凉的」，动词 vastare「使荒芜」，经古法语 waste 进入英语；同族词有 vast、devastate。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of waste start from empty land, move to the act of emptying a place, then to rubbish, to squandering, and finally to any chance that comes to nothing.
sensesIntro.cn: waste 的五个义项从荒地开始，到把地方弄空的动作，再到垃圾、挥霍，最后是一切落空的机会。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tap left dripping overnight, the water lost without ever being dirty.
core.cn: 核心意象：一夜没关紧的水龙头，水并不脏，却全部流失。

branches.en: LAND LINE: empty ground, and the act of making it empty.
branches.cn: 土地线：空旷的地，以及把它弄空的动作。

branches.en: RUBBISH LINE: what use leaves behind is thrown away.
branches.cn: 垃圾线：使用之后剩下的被丢弃。

branches.en: SQUANDER LINE: resources used so badly they become rubbish.
branches.cn: 挥霍线：资源被用得极糟，于是成了垃圾。

branches.en: CHANCE LINE: the lost thing is now possibility, not money.
branches.cn: 机会线：失去的已是可能性而非金钱。

branches.en: CONTRAST: spare keeps something; waste loses it.
branches.cn: 对照线：spare 留下东西，waste 让它失去。

intro.en: Waste is a Latin adjective and verb that English turned into three word classes at once.
intro.cn: waste 本是拉丁语的形容词与动词，英语把它一次性用成了三种词类。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is documented: vastus and vastare.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语基础有据可查：vastus 与 vastare。

definition_zh: 头脑；心智；记性；主意；留意；照看；介意
definition_en: the part of a person that thinks, feels and remembers; also memory, intention, and as a verb, to look after something or to object to it
core_image: 一个人坐在昏黄的灯下，手指按着太阳穴，屋里所有声音都退到了门外
scene: 面试进行到一半，考官忽然停下笔，问了一个与简历毫无关系的问题，房间里的空气一下子紧了。 She answered without hesitation, her mind clear and quiet under the pressure.
sceneCN: 这里是「头脑、心智」（第 1 个义项：思考与感受的那部分）；句意为她在压力之下依然头脑清楚、心里安静。图中可辨识物件：考官停下的笔、摊开的简历、安静的房间。

derivatives.zh: mind 加 -ful 构成，义为「留心的；有觉察的」
mind 加 -less 构成，义为「不用心的；无头脑的」
mind 与 set 复合，义为「思维方式；心态」
re-（再次）加 mind 的古老词干，义为「提醒；使想起」

senses.title: The thinking and feeling part of a person
senses.definition: the part of a person that thinks, feels, imagines and becomes aware of things
senses.definitionCN: 人身上用来思考、感受、想象并觉察事物的那部分
senses.example: A good question can open the mind instead of closing it.
senses.exampleCN: 一个好问题能打开人的头脑，而不是把它关上。
senses.why: Old English gemynd held memory and thought in one word, so the noun begins as the place where things are kept in awareness rather than as a plain synonym for the brain.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 gemynd 把「记忆」和「思想」放在同一个词里，所以这个名词起初指「东西被留在觉察之中的那个地方」，而不是「大脑」的简单同义词。

senses.title: To look after or keep watch on
senses.definition: to take care of a person, place or thing, or to keep watch on it for a while
senses.definitionCN: 照看某人、某处或某物，或在一段时间内看住它
senses.example: Mind the baby while I answer the door.
senses.exampleCN: 我去开门，你照看一下孩子。
senses.why: If something is held in the mind, it is being watched; from that the verb grew the sense of looking after a person or a place, as when a neighbour minds the shop.
senses.whyCN: 某物既然被放在心里，就等于被看着；动词由此长出「照看某人或某处」的意思，比如邻居替你看着店。

senses.title: To be bothered by something
senses.definition: to be troubled or annoyed by something, or to object to it, especially in questions and negatives
senses.definitionCN: 因某事而不快或恼火，或对某事表示反对，多用于疑问句与否定句
senses.example: Do you mind if I open the window?
senses.exampleCN: 我把窗户打开，你介意吗？
senses.why: To mind something in the older idiom meant to be affected by it, so the modern question about objection is really asking whether the thing touches you at all.
senses.whyCN: 在较早的用法里，to mind 某件事意为「被它影响」，所以现代那句询问是否反对的话，其实是在问这件事碰不碰到你。

senses.title: Memory and recollection
senses.definition: a person's memory, or the act of bringing something back into awareness
senses.definitionCN: 一个人的记性，或把某事重新带回觉察之中的动作
senses.example: Her name has slipped my mind again.
senses.exampleCN: 我又把她的名字忘了。
senses.why: Because the noun first meant what is held in awareness, losing a name is described as its slipping out of the mind, and the word keeps that sense of a store that can be searched.
senses.whyCN: 因为名词最初指「被留在觉察里的东西」，名字想不起来就说它从心里滑了出去，这个词便保留了「一个可以翻找的储藏处」这层意思。

senses.title: Intention or settled opinion
senses.definition: a decision or intention that a person has settled on, especially one that can be changed
senses.definitionCN: 一个人定下来的决定或打算，尤指还可以更改的那种
senses.example: He changed his mind about the trip at the last minute.
senses.exampleCN: 他在最后一刻改变了出行的主意。
senses.why: A decision is what a person settles in the mind, so making up or changing one's mind treats the mind as the place where a choice is fixed or revised.
senses.whyCN: 决定是人「在心里定下来」的东西，所以下决心或改主意，都把心当作一个把选择钉住或改写的场所。

intro.en: Mind is native English rather than borrowed: an old Germanic noun for memory and thought, related through a shared prehistoric root to the Latin word for the intellect.
intro.cn: mind 是英语本族词而非借词：一个表示记忆与思想的古老日耳曼名词，通过共同的史前词根与拉丁语表示「理智」的词相连。

items.en: A reconstructed root for thinking is generally placed behind both the Latin and the Germanic words, though the exact path is inferred rather than recorded.
items.cn: 一般认为，一个重构的「思考」词根同时位于拉丁语与日耳曼语这两组词之后，具体路径是推断出来的，并非有记录可查。

items.en: Latin mens meant mind or intellect and grew from that same root, which is why mental and mind are distant cousins rather than strangers.
items.cn: 拉丁语 mens 意为心智、理智，出自同一个词根，所以 mental 与 mind 是远亲，而不是陌生人。

items.en: Germanic speakers formed a noun for memory and thought from the root; the reconstructed form is generally written with an old prefix ga-.
items.cn: 日耳曼语使用者由这个词根造出表示记忆与思想的名词，一般认为它带有一个古老的前缀 ga-，写作重构形式。

items.en: Old English gemynd covered memory, thought and the seat of both, and the ge- prefix later dropped away.
items.cn: 古英语 gemynd 兼指记忆、思想以及承载二者的所在，前缀 ge- 后来脱落。

items.en: Modern English mind keeps the noun senses of thought, memory and intention and adds verb senses of caring, watching and objecting.
items.cn: 现代英语的 mind 保留思想、记忆、意向等名词义，又添上照看、留心、反对等动词义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the English words built on the same mind; the near-meaning group gathers the body part, the faculty, the focus and the settled view that people confuse with it.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在同一个 mind 上的英语词；近义组收容易被它混淆的身体器官、心智能力、注意力与定见。

entries.definition: Full of mind in the sense of paying attention, alert and considerate.
entries.definitionCN: 在「留心」的意义上充满 mind，即警觉而体贴的。

entries.definition: Without mind, meaning done with no thought or care behind it.
entries.definitionCN: 没有 mind，指做事不带思考或不在意。

entries.definition: A settled way of thinking, a mind set in a particular position.
entries.definitionCN: 固定下来的思维方式，把心思摆在一个特定位置上。

entries.definition: To put something back into someone's mind, built with the prefix re-.
entries.definitionCN: 用前缀 re- 构成，把某事重新放回某人的心里。

entries.definition: The physical organ inside the skull, a body part rather than the thinking self.
entries.definitionCN: 颅骨里的实体器官，是身体的一部分，而不是思考的主体。

entries.definition: The faculty that stores and brings back what was known.
entries.definitionCN: 储存并唤回已知之事的那个能力。

entries.definition: The act of holding mental focus on one thing at a time.
entries.definitionCN: 一次把心思集中在一件事上的动作。

entries.definition: A view a person holds, whether or not it has been settled into a decision.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人所持的看法，无论是否已成为决定。

normalIntro.en: The word is native Germanic, and its family keeps returning to what is held in awareness, whether that is a memory, a watch kept on something, or a view that can be changed.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是日耳曼本族词，同族词反复回到「被留在觉察里的东西」——无论那是一段记忆、对某物的看守，还是一个可以更改的看法。

normal.en: Old English gemynd meant memory before it meant thought, which is why keep in mind sounds like storing something rather than reasoning about it.
normal.cn: 古英语 gemynd 先指记忆，后指思想，所以 keep in mind 听起来更像把东西存起来，而不是对它推理。

normal.en: Latin mens and English mind come from the same old root, so mental is a relative and not a borrowed stranger.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 mens 与英语 mind 出自同一个古老词根，所以 mental 是亲戚，不是借来的陌生人。

normal.en: Mindful adds -ful, full of mind, and describes someone whose attention is fully present in the room.
normal.cn: mindful 加 -ful，意为「充满 mind」，形容一个人的注意力完全在场。

normal.en: Mindless adds -less, without mind, and describes action done with no thought behind it.
normal.cn: mindless 加 -less，意为「没有 mind」，形容做事背后不带思考。

normal.en: The verb mind began as keeping something in the mind, then split into watching over it and being troubled by it.
normal.cn: 动词 mind 从「把某物留在心里」出发，随后分成「看住它」与「被它困扰」两条路。

abstract.en: A word that begins as memory and ends as objection shows how much of thinking is really about what we cannot put down.
abstract.cn: 一个从记忆出发、到介意收尾的词，说明思考里有很大一部分其实是关于放不下的东西。

abstract.en: To mind a child and to mind the noise are the same verb, because care and irritation both begin with attention.
abstract.cn: 照看孩子与介意噪音是同一个动词，因为关心和恼火都从注意力开始。

abstract.en: Changing one's mind is not a failure of the word but its oldest freedom, a place where a choice can still be moved.
abstract.cn: 改主意不是这个词的失灵，而是它最老的自由——那个选择仍可被挪动的地方。

examples.en: The news opened her mind to a side of the story she had never considered.
examples.cn: 这条新闻让她看到了故事里从未想过的一面。

examples.en: Mind the baby while I answer the door.
examples.cn: 我去开门，你照看一下孩子。

examples.en: He changed his mind about the trip at the last minute.
examples.cn: 他在最后一刻改变了出行的主意。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「埋的」——把心事埋在心底；mind 既是头脑，也是介意与照看。

root: 古英语 gemynd（记忆、思想），源于日耳曼语中带前缀 ga- 的「思考」名词，与拉丁语 mens（心智）同出一个重构的史前词根。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the inner place where things are kept in awareness; from it come memory, attention, intention, and the verb senses of watching over something and being troubled by it.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「东西被留在觉察之中的内心之处」；记忆、注意力、意向，以及「看住某物」与「被某物困扰」这两个动词义，都从这里分出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person alone under a dim lamp, fingers pressed to the temple, every sound shut outside the door.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人独自坐在昏黄的灯下，手指按着太阳穴，所有声音都关在门外。

branches.en: a room lit by one lamp where all sound stops at the door
branches.cn: 一盏灯照着的房间，所有声音都停在门外

branches.en: a name that will not come back however hard one searches
branches.cn: 怎么翻找也想不起来的一个名字

branches.en: a neighbour watching the counter for an hour
branches.cn: 邻居替他看一小时柜台

branches.en: a question that makes a person pause before answering
branches.cn: 一个让人停顿一下才回答的问题

branches.en: a decision rewritten in the last minute
branches.cn: 最后一刻被改写的决定

intro.en: The word stands on an Old English noun of memory, an old Germanic prefix that fell away, a Latin cousin for the intellect, and English endings that build attention and the lack of it.
intro.cn: 这个词由古英语表示记忆的名词、一个后来脱落的老日耳曼前缀、一个指理智的拉丁语亲戚，以及构成「留心」与「不留心」的英语词尾共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies a close cousin rather than a parent: mens names the intellect from the same prehistoric thinking root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供的是近亲而不是父辈：mens 出自同一个史前「思考」词根，指理智。

definition_zh: 嗓音；声音；意见；发言权；语态
definition_en: the sound made when a person speaks or sings, using the vocal cords
core_image: 喉咙里的声带一收一放，空气被推成能辨认出是谁的声音
scene: 电话那头只说了半句，他就听出是谁，那个声音听过太多次了。 Her voice was so low on the phone that I could hardly hear her.
sceneCN: 这里 voice 是「嗓音」（第 1 个义项：说话或唱歌时嗓子发出的声音）；句意为她在电话里的声音低得几乎听不见。声带一收一放的那幅画就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 嗓音；声音；意见；发言权；语态

derivatives.zh: 有声的；浊音的
无声的；清音的；无发言权的
浊化；配音
声音的；发声的
发声；用言语表达

senses.title: The sound of speaking or singing
senses.definition: the sound produced in the throat when a person speaks, sings or shouts
senses.definitionCN: 人说话、唱歌或喊叫时在喉部发出的声音
senses.example: Her voice was so low on the phone that I could hardly hear her.
senses.exampleCN: 她在电话里的声音低得几乎听不见。
senses.why: The Latin word for voice named the sound itself before it named anything figurative.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语里的这个词，先指声音本身，之后才被引申他用。

senses.title: An opinion expressed
senses.definition: the opinion of a person or a group, especially as expressed aloud
senses.definitionCN: 人或群体的意见，尤指说出来的
senses.example: The voice of the staff was finally heard at the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 员工的声音终于在会上被听到了。
senses.why: What is said aloud is the voice of the one saying it, so the sound stands for the view.
senses.whyCN: 说出口的话就是说话者的声音，于是声音代替了观点。

senses.title: The right to speak and be counted
senses.definition: the right or chance to express an opinion and influence a decision
senses.definitionCN: 表达意见并影响决定的权利或机会
senses.example: Students now have a voice in how the library is run.
senses.exampleCN: 学生如今在图书馆的管理上有发言权。
senses.why: If an opinion is a voice, being allowed to speak is having a voice; the right follows from the sound.
senses.whyCN: 如果意见就是声音，那么被允许开口就是有声音，权利从声音里推演出来。

senses.title: The verb, to put into words
senses.definition: to express a feeling or opinion in words
senses.definitionCN: 用言语表达感受或意见
senses.example: She voiced doubts that no one else dared to raise.
senses.exampleCN: 她说出了别人不敢提的疑问。
senses.why: English turns many nouns into verbs without change, so the thing you have can become the thing you do.
senses.whyCN: 英语常让名词原封不动地变作动词，于是你拥有的东西就变成你做的动作。

senses.title: A grammatical form
senses.definition: in grammar, the form that shows whether the subject acts or is acted upon
senses.definitionCN: 语法中表示主语是施动还是受动的形式
senses.example: The report was rewritten in the passive voice.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告改用了被动语态。
senses.why: Roman grammarians spoke of the verb’s kinds of vox, and the term was carried into English grammar.
senses.whyCN: 罗马语法学家谈论动词的种种 vox，这个术语被带入英语语法。

senses.title: In music and phonetics, the singing part
senses.definition: a line of music for singing, or the buzzing quality of certain speech sounds
senses.definitionCN: 音乐中供唱的声部，或某些语音的带声性质
senses.example: The four voices came in one after another, none too loud.
senses.exampleCN: 四个声部依次进入，都不太响。
senses.why: A part written for singers takes the name of what singers use, and phonetics borrows it for the same reason.
senses.whyCN: 写给歌者的声部取用了歌者所用之物的名字，语音学也出于同样理由借用它。

intro.en: Voice comes from Latin vox, the word for voice, through Old French voiz.
intro.cn: voice 来自拉丁语 vox（声音、话语），经古法语 voiz 传入英语。

items.en: Vox meant both the voice and what it says, and it was used for a call or an order.
items.cn: vox 既指声音，也指声音说出的话，还用作呼喊或命令。

items.en: Roman grammarians used vox to describe the forms of the verb, and the idea of grammatical voice starts here.
items.cn: 罗马语法学家用 vox 描述动词的形式，语法上的「语态」这一观念在此起步。

items.en: Old French voiz carried the word, and the spelling was fixed in English as voice.
items.cn: 古法语 voiz 把这个词带过来，英语定下 voice 的拼法。

items.en: English extended it from sound to opinion, then to the right to speak: a voice in the matter.
items.cn: 英语把它从声音扩展到意见，再扩展到发言的权利：在这件事上有声音。

items.en: Printing and later broadcasting made the voice of the people a familiar phrase.
items.cn: 印刷术与后来的广播使「人民的声音」成为常见说法。

note.en: The first group gathers the calling and voicing family, the second the words for sound and for speech rights.
note.cn: 第一组收发声与呼叫的词族，第二组收表示声音与发言权的词。

entries.definition: The plural and the third person singular.
entries.definitionCN: 复数与第三人称单数形式

entries.definition: Uttered aloud, or produced with the vocal cords buzzing.
entries.definitionCN: 说出口的；浊音的

entries.definition: Relating to the voice, and also outspoken.
entries.definitionCN: 声音的；直言不讳的

entries.definition: A speech sound made with an open mouth.
entries.definitionCN: 元音，同一词根的旧词

entries.definition: Anything the ear can hear, voices included.
entries.definitionCN: 声音，范围更广

entries.definition: The colour or feeling of a voice.
entries.definitionCN: 语调；语气

entries.definition: A view held, whether spoken or not.
entries.definitionCN: 意见

entries.definition: The absence of any voice.
entries.definitionCN: 沉默，与声音相对

normalIntro.en: One Latin noun for the voice supplies the sound, the opinion, the right to speak, the verb and the grammar.
normalIntro.cn: 一个拉丁名词同时供给了声音、意见、发言权、动词形式与语法术语。

normal.en: Voice is both what comes out and the right to let it come out.
normal.cn: voice 既是发出的声音，也是允许发出的权利。

normal.en: Raise your voice is louder; find your voice is braver.
normal.cn: raise your voice 是提高音量，find your voice 是敢于表达。

normal.en: The verb is regular: voiced, voicing.
normal.cn: 动词变化规则：voiced、voicing。

normal.en: The passive voice moves the doer to the end.
normal.cn: 被动语态把施动者挪到句末。

normal.en: Vocal and vowel come from the same root.
normal.cn: vocal 与 vowel 同根。

abstract.en: See a throat move once and a room go quiet.
abstract.cn: 想喉咙动一下，房间就静下来。

abstract.en: Hear a phone voice and know the speaker at once.
abstract.cn: 听电话里的声音，立刻认出是谁。

abstract.en: Picture a raised hand that is given the floor.
abstract.cn: 想一只举起的手被准许发言。

examples.en: He lowered his voice so the children would not hear.
examples.cn: 他压低声音，免得孩子听见。

examples.en: Local residents have no voice in the planning process.
examples.cn: 当地居民在规划过程中没有发言权。

examples.en: She voiced her concern about the new rules.
examples.cn: 她说出了对新规定的担忧。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我嘶」——嗓子一使劲，我嘶了一声，屋里人都回头看。

root: 拉丁语 vox（声音；话语）→ 古法语 voiz → 英语 voice；同源词有 vocal、vowel、vocation。

sensesIntro.en: The word runs from the sound in the throat to an opinion, to the right to speak, to the verb of saying, to grammar and music.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从喉咙里的声音一路走到意见、发言权、动词「道出」，再到语法与音乐。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: vocal cords pushing air into a known sound.
core.cn: 核心意象：声带把空气推成熟悉的声音。

branches.en: The sound branch: a low voice on the phone.
branches.cn: 声音分支：电话里低低的嗓音。

branches.en: The opinion branch: staff heard at last.
branches.cn: 意见分支：员工终于被听到。

branches.en: The rights branch: students in library decisions.
branches.cn: 权利分支：学生在图书馆事务中的作用。

branches.en: The language branch: voiced doubts and the passive form.
branches.cn: 语言分支：道出的疑问与被动形式。

branches.en: The music branch: four parts entering one by one.
branches.cn: 音乐分支：四个声部依次进入。

intro.en: The voicing root voc- takes -al, -ize and -ation, and appears in voice, vocal and vowel.
intro.cn: 发声词根 voc- 加 -al、-ize、-ation 等后缀，出现在 voice、vocal、vowel 之中。

latinIntro.en: Latin vox with its stem voc- is recorded, and so is the adjective vocalis.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vox 及其词干 voc- 有文献记录，形容词 vocalis 亦然。

items.example: It is the root of the family.
The noun itself came into English.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词本身进入了英语。

definition_zh: 收藏品；收集；一批（收藏的东西）；募捐
definition_en: a group of things gathered together, often kept and shown; the act of collecting
core_image: 一整柜亲手攒下的宝贝
scene: 书柜最下层摆满我攒了三年的卡片。 My card collection fills the lowest shelf of the bookcase.
sceneCN: 这里 collection 是「收藏品」（第 1 个义项：攒在一起的一批东西）；句意是我的卡片收藏摆满了书柜最下层。

derivatives.zh: 本词的动词基础，义为「收集」
由 collect 加 -or 构成，义为「收藏家；收集者」
由 collect 加 -ive 构成，义为「集体的」

senses.title: A group of gathered things
senses.definition: things of one kind gathered and kept together
senses.definitionCN: 同一类东西被收集保存在一起
senses.example: Her seashell collection covers the windowsill.
senses.exampleCN: 她的贝壳收藏摆满了窗台。
senses.why: Gathered pieces make a family under one name.
senses.whyCN: 聚拢的一件件东西构成一个大家族。

senses.title: The act of gathering
senses.definition: the activity of collecting things or money
senses.definitionCN: 收集东西或钱款的行为
senses.example: The collection of rubbish starts at seven.
senses.exampleCN: 垃圾收取从七点开始。
senses.why: The action itself, not just the result, gets the name.
senses.whyCN: 不仅结果，行为本身也叫这个名字。

senses.title: Money gathered for a purpose
senses.definition: money collected from people for a cause
senses.definitionCN: 为某事从人们那里收集的钱
senses.example: The class raised fifty yuan in one collection.
senses.exampleCN: 一次募捐全班就筹了五十元。
senses.why: Coins from many hands pile into one sum.
senses.whyCN: 众人之手投入的钱币汇成一堆。

intro.en: Collection is collect with a noun ending.
intro.cn: collection 就是 collect 加名词后缀。

items.en: Latin colligere means to gather together: col- (together) plus legere (to gather).
items.cn: 拉丁语 colligere 意为聚拢：col-（一起）加 legere（收集）。

items.en: Its past form collectus kept the meaning of gathered.
items.cn: 其过去分词 collectus 保留了「被聚拢」之义。

items.en: Old French carried collecter into European use.
items.cn: 古法语把相关动词带入欧洲通用语。

items.en: English formed collection in the late Middle Ages.
items.cn: 英语在中世纪晚期形成 collection。

items.en: Later it grew senses for art, stamps and charity money.
items.cn: 后来它发展出艺术、邮票和善款的义项。

note.en: Words that gather, group and pile.
note.cn: 聚拢、成组、成堆的词。

entries.definition: verb: to gather things
entries.definitionCN: 收集（同根动词）

entries.definition: a person who collects
entries.definitionCN: 收藏家

entries.definition: shared by a group
entries.definitionCN: 集体的

entries.definition: a school; same Latin gather idea but different word
entries.definitionCN: 学院（同源拉丁概念）

entries.definition: a set of things or people
entries.definitionCN: 组；群

entries.definition: a complete group of matching things
entries.definitionCN: 一套；一组

entries.definition: a messy pile
entries.definitionCN: 堆

entries.definition: to spread in all directions
entries.definitionCN: 散开

normalIntro.en: Break the word: col + lect + ion.
normalIntro.cn: 拆词：col 加 lect 加 ion。

normal.en: col- means together.
normal.cn: 前缀 col- 表示一起。

normal.en: lect means gather.
normal.cn: 词根 lect 表示收集。

normal.en: -ion turns the verb into a noun.
normal.cn: -ion 把动词变成名词。

normal.en: a stamp collection is stamps kept together.
normal.cn: stamp collection 是保存在一起的邮票。

normal.en: the collector loves his collection.
normal.cn: 收藏家热爱自己的收藏。

abstract.en: Picture badges lined up on a velvet board.
abstract.cn: 想象徽章整齐排在丝绒板上。

abstract.en: Picture coins from many countries in one glass jar.
abstract.cn: 想象玻璃罐里各国的硬币。

abstract.en: Picture money dropping into a red charity box.
abstract.cn: 想象钱落进红色募捐箱。

examples.en: His stamp collection now has over two hundred pieces.
examples.cn: 他的集邮册已有两百多张。

examples.en: The collection of old batteries helps the environment.
examples.cn: 回收旧电池有利于环境。

examples.en: Our collection for the zoo bought two new parrots.
examples.cn: 我们为动物园的募捐买了两只新鹦鹉。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「磕来克身」——收藏家磕磕绊绊也把宝贝「克」意弄来聚在身边，所以「磕来克身」= collection。

root: 拉丁语 col-（一起）+ legere（收集）→ collectus → 英语 collect + -ion。collect、collector、elect（选出）同根。

sensesIntro.en: The gathered pile, the gathering act and the gathered money.
sensesIntro.cn: 聚拢的物、收集的行为与募来的钱。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: many things pulled into one place
core.cn: 核心意象：万物聚于一处

branches.en: Treasures kept on shelves
branches.cn: 摆在架上的珍藏

branches.en: The work of gathering
branches.cn: 收集的劳动

branches.en: Coins given for good causes
branches.cn: 为善事捐出的硬币

branches.en: A hobby built piece by piece
branches.cn: 一件件积累的爱好

branches.en: Rubbish, rent and charity rounds
branches.cn: 收取垃圾、房租与善款

intro.en: The lect- root family gathers words about choosing and collecting.
intro.cn: lect- 词族收纳了关于选择与收集的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin legere, to gather or pick, powers the family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 legere（收集、挑选）驱动词族。

items.example: Collection is the act or pile of collecting.
items.exampleCN: collection 指收集行为或成果。

definition_zh: 足够的；充足的；足够地；相当；够了
definition_en: as much or as many as is needed; to the necessary degree
core_image: 装满的水杯：水位刚好到需要的刻度线
scene: 水壶咕嘟作响，妈妈看着杯子水线到了刻度。 There is enough hot water for everyone's tea.
sceneCN: 这里 enough 是「足够的」（第 1 个义项：数量达到需要）；句意是热水够每个人泡茶。

derivatives.zh: 较罕见派生词，义为「充足状态；够用」
加否定前缀 in- 的形容词，义为「不足的」（由 sufficient 变形）

senses.title: As much as is needed
senses.definition: as much or as many of something as is required
senses.definitionCN: 数量或程度达到所需要的量
senses.example: We have enough chairs for all the guests.
senses.exampleCN: 我们的椅子够所有客人坐。
senses.why: The word comes from a Germanic root meaning to reach or suffice, so the image is a container filled to the needed line.
senses.whyCN: 该词来自日耳曼语词根，意为「达到、满足」，画面是容器刚好装到需要的刻度。

senses.title: To the necessary degree
senses.titleCN: 足够地；达到需要的程度
senses.definition: to the degree that something is necessary or wanted
senses.definitionCN: 达到必要或期望的程度
senses.example: He is old enough to travel alone.
senses.exampleCN: 他年龄够大，可以独自旅行。
senses.why: Used after adjectives, enough measures how far a quality has climbed up the scale toward the needed mark.
senses.whyCN: enough 放在形容词后，衡量某种性质沿刻度爬到所需位置的程度。

senses.title: Quite or rather
senses.definition: fairly or to a noticeable degree, often to soften a remark
senses.definitionCN: 相当的程度，常用来缓和语气
senses.example: The film was interesting enough, but not exciting.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影还算有趣，但不刺激。
senses.why: A full cup can still be just ordinary, so enough also works as a mild degree word.
senses.whyCN: 满杯也可能只是平平无奇，于是 enough 也可以作程度温和的副词。

senses.title: A sufficient amount
senses.definition: the amount that is needed; as much as necessary
senses.definitionCN: 所需的数量；必需的量
senses.example: Enough has been said about the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 关于这个计划说得够多了。
senses.why: When the thing itself is left unstated, enough stands alone as a noun for the filled measure.
senses.whyCN: 当所谈之物不必点明时，enough 单独作名词，代表那满刻度的量。

intro.en: Enough comes from Old English about filling or reaching a measure. It is a purely Germanic word with close cousins in other Germanic languages.
intro.cn: enough 来自古英语，与「填满、达到量度」有关。它是纯粹的日耳曼语词，在其他日耳曼语言中有近亲。

items.en: The reconstructed root meant 'to reach, to suffice', seen in related Germanic words for content and sufficiency.
items.cn: 重构的日耳曼语词根意为「达到、满足」，见于表示满足、充足的日耳曼语同族词。

items.en: Old English genoh meant 'enough, in sufficient quantity', built from ge- (together) plus the root nah.
items.cn: 古英语 genoh 意为「足够、数量充分」，由 ge-（一起）加词根 nah 构成。

items.en: Middle English spelled it inoh and enow, and the plural enow survived in poetry for 'enough people'.
items.cn: 中古英语拼写为 inoh 和 enow，复数 enow 在诗歌里留存，表示「足够多的人」。

items.en: The modern form enough fixed its spelling in the fifteenth century, keeping the silent gh from the older pronunciation.
items.cn: 现代拼写 enough 在十五世纪定型，gh 不发音，保留了古音的痕迹。

items.en: The idiom sure enough, meaning 'as expected', is recorded from the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 习语 sure enough「果然」最早见于十七世纪的记录。

note.en: The first group collects Germanic look-alikes with the same shape; the second collects near meanings about sufficiency.
note.cn: 第一组收集形近的日耳曼语词；第二组收集与「充足」相关的近义词。

entries.definition: an old plural form of enough, now found only in literature
entries.definitionCN: enough 的古体复数，如今只见于文学作品。

entries.definition: comfortable and warm; only similar in ending, not related in root
entries.definitionCN: 温暖舒适的；只是词尾拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: a conjunction meaning although; shares the -ough letter pattern but not the root
entries.definitionCN: 虽然；共有 -ough 拼写模式，但词源不同。

entries.definition: formal word for as much as is needed
entries.definitionCN: 足够的（正式用语）。多用于书面语。

entries.definition: more than enough, often large in size or amount
entries.definitionCN: 充裕的；丰富的。强调超出需要。

entries.definition: just enough for the purpose, sometimes barely so
entries.definitionCN: 够用的；勉强够的。强调达到基本要求。

normalIntro.en: Five concrete hooks built from spelling, sound and real usage.
normalIntro.cn: 五条基于拼写、读音与真实用法的具体联想。

normal.en: e plus nough: nough sounds like a need that stops complaining once served.
normal.cn: e + nough：nough 谐音「闹服」——需求被满足，闹够了就服了。

normal.en: Compare old enough to go: enough follows the adjective.
normal.cn: 对比例句：old enough to go（够大能去），enough 在形容词后面。

normal.en: Learn sure enough and not enough as a positive-negative pair.
normal.cn: sure enough 果然；not enough 不够，一正一反成对记。

normal.en: Enough matches German genug; the g corresponds to gh.
normal.cn: enough 与 German 里的 genug 同源，g 对应 gh，德英对照好记。

normal.en: The sound hints at taking once and having enough, for spelling only.
normal.cn: 谐音：「一拿 enough」——一拿就够，帮助拼读，不是词源。

abstract.en: Picture the water level stopping exactly on the dotted line.
abstract.cn: 画面：杯中水位刚好停在虚线上，一滴不多一滴不少。

abstract.en: Feel the moment you put down your chopsticks, full and done.
abstract.cn: 感觉：吃饱后放下筷子的那一刻，身体说 enough。

abstract.en: Draw a line in the air; where the line lands is the needed amount.
abstract.cn: 动作：伸手指在空中画一条线，线到之处就是需要的量。

examples.en: There is not enough milk for breakfast.
examples.cn: 牛奶不够早餐用的。

examples.en: She is tall enough to reach the top shelf.
examples.cn: 她个子够高，能够到最上层的架子。

examples.en: Sure enough, the train arrived on time.
examples.cn: 果然，火车准时到达。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「闹夫」——不闹了，丈夫总算把东西拿够，谐音帮助拼读，不是词源。

root: enough 来自古英语 genōh（ge- 表完成 + nōh「达到、满足」），与德语 genug、荷兰语 genoeg 同源，是纯粹的日耳曼语词，与拉丁语系词根无关。

sensesIntro.en: Enough works as adjective, adverb and noun, all around the single image of a measure that is filled to the mark.
sensesIntro.cn: enough 可作形容词、副词与名词，全部围绕「量器装到刻度线」这一个意象展开。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a container filled exactly to the needed line.
core.cn: 核心意象：容器刚好装到所需刻度线。

branches.en: QUANTITY BRANCH
branches.cn: 足够的椅子、足够的钱、足够的某物。

branches.en: DEGREE BRANCH
branches.cn: old enough、strong enough，放在形容词之后。

branches.en: MILD DEGREE
branches.cn: interesting enough 表示温和、公允的评价。

branches.en: STANDALONE AMOUNT
branches.cn: 名词省略时单独使用的 enough。

branches.en: SATISFACTION BRANCH
branches.cn: 不再需要更多的共同感受。

intro.en: Enough is a single Germanic word; its family lives in Germanic languages, not Latin.
intro.cn: enough 是单个日耳曼语词；其词族在日耳曼语言中，不在拉丁语中。

latinIntro.en: No Latin root applies; the family is Germanic, so the Latin entry list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 本词与拉丁词根无关，词族属于日耳曼语，因此拉丁同源词列表为空。

items.example: In genoh the prefix marked the goal being reached.
items.exampleCN: 在 genoh 中该前缀表示目标达成。

items.example: though, through and enough share the silent gh spelling.
items.exampleCN: though、through 与 enough 共享不发音的 gh。

items.example: Sufficient literally means held up to the need.
The same root appears in factory and efficient.
items.exampleCN: 该词根也见于 factory 与 efficient。

items.example: Ample means wide enough to hold more than needed.
Adequate means equal to the task.
Genug mirrors Old English genoh almost exactly.
items.exampleCN: genug 与古英语 genoh 几乎完全对应。

definition_zh: 搜索；寻找；搜查；搜寻
definition_en: to look carefully for something, to examine a place, or the act of looking
core_image: 手电筒的光柱在黑暗房间里来回移动，寻找丢失的钥匙
scene: 他们在黑暗的房间里寻找钥匙。 They searched the dark room for the key.
sceneCN: 这里 search 是「搜索；寻找」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他们在黑暗的房间里寻找钥匙。

derivatives.zh: 研究
搜索者
锐利的；彻底的
可搜索的

senses.title: To look for something
senses.definition: to look carefully for something or someone
senses.definitionCN: 仔细寻找某物或某人
senses.example: She searched for her keys.
senses.exampleCN: 她寻找她的钥匙。
senses.why: The central sense is looking for something lost or wanted.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是寻找丢失或想要的东西。

senses.title: To examine a place
senses.definition: to examine a place or person thoroughly
senses.definitionCN: 彻底检查某个地方或某个人
senses.example: The police searched the house.
senses.exampleCN: 警察搜查了那所房子。
senses.why: Looking for something becomes a formal examination of a place.
senses.whyCN: 寻找某物变成对场所的正式检查。

senses.title: An act of looking
senses.definition: an attempt to find something
senses.definitionCN: 寻找某物的尝试
senses.example: The search took two hours.
senses.exampleCN: 搜寻花了两个小时。
senses.why: The verb becomes a noun for the whole effort.
senses.whyCN: 动词转为表示整个努力过程的名词。

intro.en: Search comes from Old French cerchier, from Latin circare, to go around.
intro.cn: search 源自古法语 cerchier，来自拉丁语 circare（绕行）。

items.en: Circare meant to go around or wander over.
items.cn: circare 意为绕行或走遍。

items.en: Cerchier meant to look through a place.
items.cn: cerchier 意为搜遍一个地方。

items.en: Serchen meant to examine or look for.
items.cn: serchen 意为检查或寻找。

items.en: Search named an official examination.
items.cn: search 指正式检查。

items.en: Search covers looking, examining, and online finding.
items.cn: 现代英语中 search 涵盖寻找、搜查与网络检索。

note.en: Search is compared with similar-looking words and with verbs for seeking.
note.cn: 把 search 与形近词以及表示寻找的动词作比较。

entries.definition: careful study to find facts
entries.definitionCN: 研究

entries.definition: a building for worship
entries.definitionCN: 教堂

entries.definition: a place where a bird rests
entries.definitionCN: 栖木

entries.definition: to try to find or obtain
entries.definitionCN: 寻找；寻求

entries.definition: to search for something actively
entries.definitionCN: 搜寻；追猎

entries.definition: to travel through and examine
entries.definitionCN: 探索

normalIntro.en: Search is looking for something, and also the whole attempt.
normalIntro.cn: search 是寻找某物，也指整个寻找过程。

normal.en: Search for your keys.
normal.cn: 寻找你的钥匙。

normal.en: A search engine finds pages.
normal.cn: 搜索引擎查找网页。

normal.en: In search of means looking for.
normal.cn: in search of 意为寻找。

normal.en: Police search a house.
normal.cn: 警察搜查房屋。

normal.en: Research adds re to search.
normal.cn: research 是在 search 前加 re。

abstract.en: Search began as going around a place.
abstract.cn: search 最初指绕遍一个地方。

abstract.en: Looking for an object and examining a place share one verb.
abstract.cn: 找东西与查地方共用一个动词。

abstract.en: The noun turns a moment of looking into a process.
abstract.cn: 名词义把一次寻找变成一段过程。

examples.en: She searched for her keys.
examples.cn: 她寻找她的钥匙。

examples.en: The police searched the house.
examples.cn: 警察搜查了那所房子。

examples.en: The search took two hours.
examples.cn: 搜寻花了两个小时。

dict_mnemonic.text: search 源自拉丁语 circare（绕行），原义是「走遍一个地方去找」，所以既指寻找，也指搜查。

root: 源自古法语 cerchier，来自拉丁语 circare（绕行），核心义「走遍某处寻找」。

sensesIntro.en: Search means to look for something, to examine a place, or the act of looking.
sensesIntro.cn: search 意为寻找某物、搜查某地，或搜寻行为。

core.en: Moving through a place to find something.
core.cn: 走遍某地以寻找某物。

branches.en: Looking for a lost or wanted thing.
branches.cn: 寻找丢失或想要的东西。

branches.en: Examining a place for evidence.
branches.cn: 为寻找证据而检查某地。

branches.en: The effort as a whole.
branches.cn: 整个寻找过程。

branches.en: Both senses involve careful looking.
branches.cn: 两个义项都涉及仔细查看。

branches.en: The action and the effort share one word.
branches.cn: 动作与过程共用一个词。

intro.en: Search forms words for research, people, and tools.
intro.cn: search 构成表示研究、人物与工具的词汇。

latinIntro.en: Latin circare, to go around, is the distant source.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 circare（绕行）是远源。

items.meaning: to look for, or an attempt to find

items.example: She gave him a searching look.

items.meaning: a service that finds web pages
items.example: The search engine returned many results.
items.exampleCN: 搜索引擎返回了许多结果。

items.example: A search party combed the woods.

definition_zh: 发烧；发热；热病；狂热；亢奋
definition_en: a body temperature higher than normal because of illness, a disease marked by this, or a state of intense excitement
core_image: 额头滚烫，脸颊发红，整个身体像一团过热的炉火
scene: 深夜的孩子满脸通红，母亲把体温计贴上额头。 The nurse checked whether the fever had broken.
sceneCN: 这里 fever 是名词，指「发烧」这一症状，对应第 1 个义项；句意为护士查看烧是否已经退去。

pos.zh: 发烧；热病；狂热；一时的亢奋

derivatives.zh: 发烧的；狂热的（fever 加形容词后缀 -ish，指体温高或情绪亢奋）
发烧地；狂热地（feverish 加副词后缀 -ly）
发烧的；焦躁的（fever 的过去分词作形容词，指受热或受扰的）

senses.title: A higher-than-normal body temperature
senses.definition: a body temperature above the normal level, usually from illness
senses.definitionCN: 体温高出正常水平，通常由疾病引起
senses.example: The child has a slight fever.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子有点低烧。
senses.why: The body burns hotter than it should, so the word names the heat itself.
senses.whyCN: 身体烧得比该有的温度高，词首先命名这股热度。

senses.title: A disease marked by fever
senses.definition: an illness in which fever is the main sign
senses.definitionCN: 以发热为主要征兆的疾病
senses.example: Scarlet fever once frightened every parent.
senses.exampleCN: 猩红热曾令每位家长恐惧。
senses.why: When the symptom defines the sickness, the sickness takes the symptom's name.
senses.whyCN: 当症状定义疾病，疾病便以症状为名。

senses.title: Intense excitement or agitation
senses.definition: a state of great excitement or nervous energy
senses.definitionCN: 极度兴奋或躁动的状态
senses.example: The city was in a fever of excitement before the match.
senses.exampleCN: 比赛前全城兴奋若狂。
senses.why: Excitement heats the mind the way illness heats the body.
senses.whyCN: 亢奋使头脑发热，正如疾病使身体发热。

senses.title: A short-lived craze
senses.definition: a wave of enthusiasm that sweeps through people for a time
senses.definitionCN: 一时席卷人群的热情浪潮
senses.example: Gold fever sent thousands west.
senses.exampleCN: 淘金热把成千上万的人推向西部。
senses.why: A craze is a fever of the crowd: it burns hot and passes.
senses.whyCN: 热潮是群体的发烧：烧得猛，退得也快。

intro.en: Fever comes straight from Latin febris 'heat of illness', borrowed through Old French fievre and reshaped into English spelling.
intro.cn: fever 直接源自拉丁语 febris「病热」，经古法语 fievre 借入并改写为英语拼写。

items.en: Latin febris meant 'fever', from a root meaning 'to burn'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 febris 意为「发烧」，出自表「燃烧」的词根。

items.en: Old French fievre carried the word into Romance speech with its senses intact.
items.cn: 古法语 fievre 原义不变地把这个词带入罗曼语。

items.en: Middle English adopted fever (also fevre) for body heat and for diseases like it.
items.cn: 中古英语借入 fever（亦作 fevre），指体热及类似疾病。

items.en: The spelling settled as fever, standard in medicine and daily speech.
items.cn: 现代英语拼写定为 fever，为医学与日常通用。

items.en: Metaphorical use spread widely: election fever, gold fever, a fever of activity.
items.cn: 比喻用法广泛传播：election fever、gold fever、a fever of activity。

note.en: Look-alikes share the fe- shape; near-meaning words cover temperature, illness and excitement.
note.cn: 形近组共享 fe- 字形；近义组覆盖体温、疾病与亢奋。

entries.definition: a smaller number of; one letter changes the meaning completely
entries.definitionCN: 更少的；仅一字母之差而意义全变

entries.definition: showing strong feeling; from Latin fervere 'to boil'
entries.definitionCN: 热烈的；出自拉丁语 fervere「沸腾」

entries.definition: a boat that carries people across water
entries.definitionCN: 渡船；拼写相近但词源无关

entries.definition: the degree of heat of the body
entries.definitionCN: 体温；热度

entries.definition: high temperature or hotness
entries.definitionCN: 热；高温

entries.definition: a short-lived enthusiasm
entries.definitionCN: 一时的狂热；风尚

normalIntro.en: Five handles from the Latin root and the metaphorical uses.
normalIntro.cn: 五个来自拉丁词根与比喻用法的记忆抓手。

normal.en: feverish means fever-like: hot body or hot mood.
normal.cn: feverish 意为「像发烧一样」：身体发热或情绪亢奋。

normal.en: break a fever means the fever finally stops.
normal.cn: break a fever 表示烧终于退了。

normal.en: gold fever is the classic crowd fever: everyone rushes for the same prize.
normal.cn: gold fever 是经典的群体狂热：人人涌向同一目标。

normal.en: Latin febris is the root; English fever keeps only the heat idea.
normal.cn: 词根是拉丁语 febris；英语 fever 只保留「热」的概念。

normal.en: never confuse fever with fewer, which counts things down.
normal.cn: 别把 fever 与 fewer（更少）弄混。

abstract.en: A fever is the body's alarm fire: hot, bright, and meant to pass.
abstract.cn: 发烧是身体的报警之火：灼热、明亮，也注定退去。

abstract.en: Crowd fever is a fire that spreads without fuel.
abstract.cn: 群体狂热是不需燃料也能蔓延的火。

abstract.en: Excitement and illness share one thermometer.
abstract.cn: 亢奋与疾病共用同一支体温计。

examples.en: His fever finally broke on the third night.
examples.cn: 他的烧在第三晚终于退了。

examples.en: The whole class was in a fever before the results were posted.
examples.cn: 成绩公布前全班都处于亢奋之中。

examples.en: Doctors warned that scarlet fever was spreading in the district.
examples.cn: 医生警告猩红热正在该地区蔓延。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「肥捂热」—— 发烧的人身体肥而滚烫，需捂热降温 → fever 发烧

root: 源自拉丁语 febris「发烧」（一般认为出自表「燃烧」的词根），经古法语 fievre 进入中古英语；核心是「病中之热」，后扩展为比喻的「狂热」。

sensesIntro.en: From body heat outward to the diseases named by it, and then to excitement and crowd crazes.
sensesIntro.cn: 从体温升高出发，扩展到以其命名之疾病，再到亢奋与群体热潮。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a burning forehead, the body running hotter than it should.
core.cn: 核心意象：滚烫的额头，身体烧得超过了应有的温度。

branches.en: THE HEAT: raised body temperature.
branches.cn: 热度：升高的体温。

branches.en: THE ILLNESS: disease known by its fever.
branches.cn: 疾病：以发热闻名的病。

branches.en: THE EXCITEMENT: minds heated like bodies.
branches.cn: 亢奋：头脑如身体般发热。

branches.en: THE CRAZE: a wave that burns and fades.
branches.cn: 热潮：烧起又退去的浪潮。

branches.en: THE METAPHOR: heat transferred from body to mood.
branches.cn: 比喻：热度由身体移入情绪。

intro.en: Fever builds its family with native suffixes: feverish, fevered and their adverbs.
intro.cn: fever 用本族后缀构词：feverish、fevered 及其副词。

latinIntro.en: Latin febris stands alone in the family; related Latin fervere 'to boil' gives fervent instead.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 febris 在词族中独立；相关的 fervere「沸腾」派生的是 fervent。

items.meaning: having a fever or wild excitement

items.exampleCN: 热烈的演讲打动了他们。

items.example: She caught a fever at camp.
A high fever needs a doctor.

definition_zh: 病人；患者；有耐心的；能忍耐的
definition_en: a person receiving medical treatment, or an adjective meaning able to wait or bear difficulty without becoming angry
core_image: 诊所走廊里，老人抱着病历本等叫号
scene: 诊所走廊里，一位老人把病历本抱在胸前，等着护士叫号。 The patient waited quietly for his name to be called.
sceneCN: 这里的 patient 是「病人、患者」（第 1 个义项：正在接受诊疗的人）；句意是那位病人安静地等着叫到他的名字。图中可辨识物件：病历本、走廊长椅、诊室门。

derivatives.zh: 由 patient 加 -ly 构成，义为「耐心地」
由拉丁语 patientia 经古法语进入英语，义为「耐心」；与 patient 同源
由否定前缀 im- 加 patient 构成，义为「不耐烦的」

senses.title: A person receiving medical care
senses.definition: a person who is receiving medical treatment, especially in a hospital or clinic
senses.definitionCN: 正在接受医疗诊治的人，尤指在医院或诊所里的
senses.example: The patient waited quietly for his name to be called.
senses.exampleCN: 那位病人安静地等着叫到他的名字。
senses.why: The noun comes from the same Latin participle: a sick person is literally the one who is suffering, the one who bears the illness.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词出自同一个拉丁分词：生病的人字面上就是「正在受苦的那一个」，是承受着疾病的人。

senses.title: Able to wait without annoyance
senses.definition: able to wait for a long time or accept delay without becoming annoyed
senses.definitionCN: 能够长时间等待或接受延误而不烦躁的
senses.example: Please be patient with the new trainee.
senses.exampleCN: 请对新来的实习生耐心一些。
senses.why: The adjective names the bearing of delay, so the old sense of suffering narrows to the mild discomfort of having to wait.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词指的是对延误的承受，于是「受苦」的旧义收窄为「不得不等待」这种轻微的不适。

senses.title: Able to endure provocation calmly
senses.definition: able to bear pain, provocation or difficulty without losing calm
senses.definitionCN: 能够承受痛苦、挑衅或困难而不失镇定的
senses.example: She stayed patient under a stream of rude questions.
senses.exampleCN: 在一连串无礼的提问下，她仍然保持忍耐。
senses.why: The original Latin sense of enduring pain survives in this use, where what must be borne is not time but pressure coming from other people.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语原本「忍受痛苦」的意思在这个用法里存活下来，只是要承受的不再是时间，而是来自他人的压力。

intro.en: Patient is the present participle of Latin pati, to suffer, passed through Old French pacient; English uses the same shape for the adjective and for the sick person, while the noun patience split off from Latin patientia.
intro.cn: patient 是拉丁语 pati（忍受）的现在分词，经古法语 pacient 传入英语；英语用同一个形状既作形容词，也指病人，而名词 patience 则从拉丁语 patientia 另分出来。

items.en: Pati meant to suffer, undergo or put up with, and it is the root behind both patient and patience.
items.cn: pati 意为受苦、经历、忍受，是 patient 与 patience 共同的词根。

items.en: Patiens was the present participle, literally suffering or enduring, and it could already be used as an adjective for someone who bears things well.
items.cn: patiens 是现在分词，字面意为「忍受着的」，已经能作形容词，形容善于承受的人。

items.en: From the same participle Latin built patientia, the noun of endurance, which became the English noun patience rather than the adjective.
items.cn: 拉丁语由同一分词构成名词 patientia，表示忍耐，它后来成为英语名词 patience，而不是形容词。

items.en: Old French kept pacient as both adjective and noun, and the noun could already mean a sick person under care.
items.cn: 古法语保留 pacient，兼作形容词与名词，其中的名词已经能指接受照料的病人。

items.en: Modern English keeps patient as an adjective and as a noun for the sick, and keeps patience as the separate noun for the quality.
items.cn: 现代英语让 patient 作形容词并指病人，又让 patience 作为独立名词表示这种品质。

note.en: The look-alike group puts the same-root noun, adverb and negative beside patient so the parts of speech stay distinct; the near-meaning group gathers words for calm bearing and for the sick person.
note.cn: 形近组把同根的名词、副词与否定式摆在 patient 旁边，以便分清词性；近义组收表示平静承受的词，以及指病人的词。

entries.definition: The noun for the ability to wait or endure calmly.
entries.definitionCN: 表示平静等待或忍耐能力的名词。

entries.definition: In a manner that shows calm endurance.
entries.definitionCN: 以平静忍耐的方式。

entries.definition: Unable to bear delay or waiting calmly.
entries.definitionCN: 无法平静承受延误或等待的。

entries.definition: Quiet and not showing worry, anger or excitement.
entries.definitionCN: 平静的，不显焦虑、愤怒或激动的。

entries.definition: Willing to accept differences and things one dislikes.
entries.definitionCN: 愿意接受差异与自己不喜欢之事的。

entries.definition: Lasting for a long time, or able to bear hardship.
entries.definitionCN: 持久的，或能承受艰难的。

entries.definition: A person who is affected by an illness or a bad situation.
entries.definitionCN: 受疾病或困境影响的人。

normalIntro.en: Patient is one Latin participle doing two jobs in English, and its hooks keep the sick person and the calm bearer tied to the same root.
normalIntro.cn: patient 是同一个拉丁分词在英语里兼做两件事，记忆钩子让「病人」与「平静承受者」都系在同一个词根上。

normal.en: Pati, to suffer, is the root of both patient and patience, so the sick person and the calm waiter share one history.
normal.cn: pati（忍受）是 patient 与 patience 共同的词根，所以病人与平静等待的人共享同一段历史。

normal.en: As a noun, patient is the one who suffers an illness; as an adjective, it is the one who bears a wait. One shape, two jobs.
normal.cn: 作名词时，patient 是承受疾病的人；作形容词时，是承受等待的人。一个形状，两份工作。

normal.en: Patience is the noun from patientia, so the pair differs in part of speech and not in origin.
normal.cn: patience 是出自 patientia 的名词，所以这一对词的差别在词性，而不在来源。

normal.en: Patiently adds -ly to the adjective and describes the manner of bearing a delay.
normal.cn: patiently 给形容词加 -ly，描述承受延误的方式。

normal.en: Impatient adds im-, not, and names the refusal to keep bearing.
normal.cn: impatient 加上表示「不」的 im-，指不肯继续承受。

abstract.en: A word that names both the sick and the forbearing suggests that illness is the first school of patience.
abstract.cn: 一个词既指病人又指能忍耐的人，说明疾病是耐心的第一所学校。

abstract.en: Because the adjective and the noun share one shape, English lets a description of character stand for a person in a hospital bed.
abstract.cn: 因为形容词与名词共用一个形状，英语可以让对品性的描述直接指代病床上的人。

abstract.en: Patient care measures a system by how it treats people who can do nothing but wait.
abstract.cn: 病人护理衡量一个体系的方式，是看它如何对待那些除了等待什么也做不了的人。

examples.en: The patient waited quietly for his name to be called.
examples.cn: 那位病人安静地等着叫到他的名字。

examples.en: Please be patient with the new trainee.
examples.cn: 请对新来的实习生耐心一些。

examples.en: She stayed patient under a stream of rude questions.
examples.cn: 在一连串无礼的提问下，她仍然保持忍耐。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「陪身特」——亲人陪着身子特别弱的病人；记住 patient 是病人，也是「有耐心的」。

root: 拉丁语 pati（忍受）的现在分词 patiens 派生出 patient，既指「忍受着的（人）」，也指「病人」；同根的 patientia 则是名词 patience（耐心）的来源。patient 与 patience 同源，但 patient 主要作形容词「有耐心的」和名词「病人」，patience 只能作名词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is bearing something; the noun names the one who bears an illness, and the adjective names the one who bears delay or pressure.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是承受着某物；名词指承受疾病的人，形容词指承受延误或压力的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old man in a clinic corridor holding his folder, waiting for his name.
core.cn: 核心意象：诊所走廊里，一位老人抱着病历本，等着叫到自己的名字。

branches.en: a corridor of people holding folders
branches.cn: 走廊里抱着病历本的人们

branches.en: a nurse calling a name at a door
branches.cn: 护士在门口叫号

branches.en: a trainee told to try once more
branches.cn: 被告知再试一次的实习生

branches.en: a witness answering rude questions
branches.cn: 面对无礼提问的证人

branches.en: a bed beside a window in a ward
branches.cn: 病房里靠窗的一张床

intro.en: The word is a Latin participle reshaped by French, and English adds endings to build the adverb, the separate noun of the quality and the negative form.
intro.cn: 这个词是经法语改写的拉丁分词，英语再加词尾，造出副词、表示该品质的独立名词与否定形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin pati, patiens and patientia are all recorded, so patient has a documented ancestry shared with patience, patiently and impatient.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pati、patiens 与 patientia 均有记录，因此 patient 与 patience、patiently、impatient 共享有据可查的世系。

definition_zh: 称…的重量；重达；权衡；使烦恼
definition_en: to measure how heavy something is, to have a stated weight, and to think carefully about choices
core_image: 老式天平两端各放一只盘，指针在刻度间来回摆动最后停住
scene: 集市上卖水果的老板把袋子放上秤盘，指针一晃，最后停在一个数上，他报出价来。 The seller put the bag on the scale to weigh it and waited for the needle to settle.
sceneCN: 这里 weigh 是「称重」（第 1 个义项：测量某物有多重）；句意为摊主把袋子放上秤，等指针停稳。两端摆动的天平与指针就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 称…的重量；重达；权衡；使忧心

derivatives.zh: 重量；分量；砝码
沉重的；重要的
称量；权衡
重于；使负担过重
重量不足

senses.title: To measure weight
senses.definition: to find out how heavy something is, using a scale
senses.definitionCN: 用秤查明某物有多重
senses.example: The nurse weighed the baby at every visit.
senses.exampleCN: 护士每次来访都给婴儿称重。
senses.why: This is the core sense: the balance answers a question of heaviness.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心义：天平回答「有多重」的问题。

senses.title: To have a stated weight
senses.definition: to be of a particular heaviness
senses.definitionCN: 具有某个特定的重量
senses.example: This parcel weighs almost two kilos.
senses.exampleCN: 这个包裹重近两公斤。
senses.why: The verb takes the weight as its own measure, so no object is needed.
senses.whyCN: 动词自身带上重量，因此不需要宾语。

senses.title: To think about choices
senses.definition: to compare facts or options carefully before deciding
senses.definitionCN: 在决定前仔细比较事实或选项
senses.example: The committee weighed the risks before voting.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会在投票前权衡了风险。
senses.why: A balance holds two pans, and a mind holds two options the same way.
senses.whyCN: 天平托着两只盘，头脑也同样托着两个选择。

senses.title: To be a burden on someone
senses.definition: to trouble or oppress a person’s mind
senses.definitionCN: 使某人心里烦恼、沉重
senses.example: The decision weighed on her for weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 这个决定压在她心上好几周。
senses.why: Something heavy presses down, so worry is said to weigh on a mind.
senses.whyCN: 沉重的东西会向下压，于是忧虑被说成压在心头。

senses.title: To raise a ship’s anchor
senses.definition: of a ship, to lift the anchor before sailing
senses.definitionCN: 指船在启航前把锚拉起
senses.example: The fleet weighed anchor at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 船队在黎明起锚。
senses.why: A phrase from sailing, kept because anchor and balance share the idea of lifting.
senses.whyCN: 这是航海用语，因为起锚与天平共通「抬起」的意象而保留。

intro.en: Weigh comes from Old English wegan, to carry or to lift, the same root that gives wagon and the Latin vehere, to carry.
intro.cn: weigh 来自古英语 wegan（搬运、抬起），与 wagon 及拉丁语 vehere（运载）同根。

items.en: The root meant to move or carry a load, and weighing was done by lifting and comparing.
items.cn: 这一词根意为移动或承载，古时称量靠抬起并比较。

items.en: Wegan meant to carry, to lift and to weigh, all in one verb.
items.cn: wegan 一名兼指搬运、抬起与称量。

items.en: The spelling weigh appeared, and the past form became weighed under French-influenced habits.
items.cn: 拼写 weigh 出现，过去式在法语影响下成为 weighed。

items.en: The weighing of evidence extended the word to judgement and decision.
items.cn: 权衡证据把词义扩展到判断与决断。

items.en: Weight, the noun, came from the same root and now names the thing measured.
items.cn: 名词 weight 出自同根，如今指被测量的那份东西。

note.en: The first group shares the weigh root and shape, the second the words used in measuring and deciding.
note.cn: 第一组与 weigh 同根形近，第二组是测量与决断中的近义词。

entries.definitionCN: 重量；砝码

entries.definition: Heavy, or serious and important.
entries.definitionCN: 沉重的；重要的

entries.definition: The act of measuring or judging.

entries.definition: To find the size or amount of something.
entries.definitionCN: 测量

entries.definition: To think about something before deciding.

entries.definition: To judge the value or quality of something.

entries.definition: To load someone with a heavy duty or worry.
entries.definitionCN: 使负担

normalIntro.en: Start with the balance, then let it tilt into decisions and into worry.
normalIntro.cn: 先看天平，再让它倾斜出去，成为决断与忧虑。

normal.en: Weigh is the verb; weight is the noun.
normal.cn: weigh 是动词，weight 是名词。

normal.en: Weigh about ten kilos needs no object.
normal.cn: weigh about ten kilos 不带宾语。

normal.en: Weigh the options means put each one on the balance.
normal.cn: weigh the options 就是把每个选择放上天平。

normal.en: Weigh on someone means press down on the mind.
normal.cn: weigh on someone 是压在某人心上。

normal.en: Weigh anchor is the opposite of drop anchor.
normal.cn: weigh anchor 与 drop anchor 相反。

abstract.en: Picture a needle swinging and dying away.
abstract.cn: 想指针摆动后慢慢停住。

abstract.en: Hear the small click of a brass weight set down.
abstract.cn: 听铜砝码落下时轻轻一响。

abstract.en: Feel one side sink and the other rise.
abstract.cn: 感受一头下沉、一头升起。

examples.en: Please weigh this parcel before you post it.
examples.cn: 寄之前请称一下这个包裹。

examples.en: She weighs less than she did last year.
examples.cn: 她比去年轻了些。

examples.en: You must weigh the cost against the benefit.
examples.cn: 你必须把成本与收益权衡一下。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喂」——摊主喊一声「喂」，把袋子往秤上一放，看指针停在哪。

root: 日耳曼语词根（搬运、抬举）→ 古英语 wegan（搬、抬、称）→ weigh；同根词有 weight、wagon，拉丁语 vehere。

sensesIntro.en: The verb starts at the balance, states a weight, then moves to weighing options, to weighing on a mind, and to lifting an anchor.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个动词从天平出发，报出重量，再转为权衡选择、压在心头，最后是起锚。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a scale needle settling.
core.cn: 核心意象：停住的秤针。

branches.en: The measure branch: weighing a baby and weighing two kilos.
branches.cn: 测量分支：给婴儿称重与重两公斤。

branches.en: The judgement branch: comparing risks before a vote.
branches.cn: 判断分支：投票前比较风险。

branches.en: The burden branch: a decision that presses for weeks.
branches.cn: 负担分支：压了数周的决定。

branches.en: The sailing branch: anchor lifted at dawn.
branches.cn: 航海分支：黎明起锚。

branches.en: The scale and the mind share one image: two pans, then two choices.
branches.cn: 天平与头脑共用一个意象：两只盘，两个选择。

intro.en: Weigh takes regular endings and the noun weight from the same root.
intro.cn: weigh 用规则词尾，名词 weight 出自同一词根。

latinIntro.en: The Latin cousin vehere means to carry, and the table shows how the same image spread.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁同源词 vehere 意为运载，拉丁表展示同一意象的扩散。

definition_zh: 拉；拖；拔出；拉伤；拉力；吸引力；影响力
definition_en: to move something towards oneself or in a stated direction by using force; to remove something by drawing it out; to injure a muscle; also the force that draws, a physical attraction, and personal influence
core_image: 一个人双手攥住粗绳，脚蹬地面，把绳子一点点拽向自己
scene: 绳子另一头卡在石缝里，几个人排成一列，脚掌抵住地面，一起把劲儿往后使。 They pulled the rope until the log slid out of the mud.
sceneCN: 这里 pull 是「拉、拽」（第 1 个义项：用力把东西朝自己或某个方向移动）；句意为他们一直拉绳子，直到那根木头从泥里滑出来。图中可辨识物件：粗绳、石缝、蹬地的脚。

derivatives.zh: pull 与 over 复合，指从头上套下去穿的毛衣
pull 与 back 复合，指军队或企业的撤退、收缩
pull 加表人后缀 -er，指拉东西的人或拔取工具

senses.title: To move something towards oneself
senses.definition: to move a person or thing towards oneself or along behind oneself by using force
senses.definitionCN: 用力把人或物朝自己方向移动，或让其在身后跟着移动
senses.example: She pulled the heavy box across the floor.
senses.exampleCN: 她把那个沉重的箱子拖着在地板上移动。
senses.why: The Old English verb meant to pluck or tug at something, so the body's grip and the backward motion are both built into the word from the start.
senses.whyCN: 这个古英语动词本义是「揪、拽」，所以手握住的力道和向后移动的方向从一开始就长在词里。

senses.title: To remove something by drawing it out
senses.definition: to take something out of a place or a body by drawing it steadily away
senses.definitionCN: 通过持续往外拽，把某物从某个位置或身体里取出来
senses.example: The dentist pulled two of his teeth.
senses.exampleCN: 牙医拔掉了他两颗牙。
senses.why: Pulling in the first sense moves a whole object; aim the same motion at a part held inside something and the meaning narrows to extraction.
senses.whyCN: 第一义的拉是移动整个物体；把同样的动作对准嵌在某物内部的东西，词义就收窄为「拔出」。

senses.title: To injure a muscle by overstretching it
senses.definition: to damage a muscle or tendon by stretching it too far
senses.definitionCN: 因拉伸过度而损伤肌肉或肌腱
senses.example: He pulled a muscle in his calf during the sprint.
senses.exampleCN: 他在短跑时拉伤了小腿肌肉。
senses.why: The fibres of a muscle are drawn apart by a sudden load, and English describes that damage with the same verb it uses for drawing something apart.
senses.whyCN: 肌肉纤维被突然的负荷拽开，英语就用「往开拽」这个动词来描述这种损伤。

senses.title: A steady force that draws something
senses.definition: a force that draws an object steadily in one direction
senses.definitionCN: 把物体持续朝某个方向吸引的力
senses.example: The pull of the moon lifts the sea into tides.
senses.exampleCN: 月球的引力把海水拉起，形成潮汐。
senses.why: Once the verb names the act, the noun can name the force behind it, so a rope, a magnet and the moon all exert a pull.
senses.whyCN: 动词一旦指这个动作，名词就能指动作背后的力，于是绳子、磁铁和月亮都能产生 pull。

senses.title: Personal influence or attraction
senses.definition: the power to influence events or attract people, especially through connections
senses.definitionCN: 影响事情或吸引他人的力量，尤指凭借人脉关系
senses.example: His family has a lot of pull in this town.
senses.exampleCN: 他家在这个镇上很有门路。
senses.why: A person with connections can draw decisions the way a rope draws a load, so the physical sense extends to social leverage and charm.
senses.whyCN: 有门路的人能像绳子拉动货物那样牵动决定，于是物理义延伸到社会上的影响力与魅力。

intro.en: Pull is an Old English verb of Germanic stock, first recorded as pullian with the sense of plucking or tugging; it has no reliable Latin cognate, so the Latin comparison is left empty.
intro.cn: pull 是源自日耳曼语族的古英语动词，最早写作 pullian，意为「揪、拽」；它没有可靠的拉丁同族词，因此拉丁对照留空。

items.en: Pullian is recorded in Old English with the sense of plucking wool or tugging at something, and it already implies a hand closing on a thing.
items.cn: 古英语中的 pullian 意为揪羊毛、拽东西，词里已经含有「手攥住某物」的意思。

items.en: The verb belongs to the Germanic layer of English rather than to the Latin layer, and related forms appear in several Germanic languages.
items.cn: 这个动词属于英语的日耳曼语层而非拉丁语层，在几种日耳曼语言中都有相关形式。

items.en: Middle English kept the verb and widened it from plucking to any steady drawing motion, including pulling a cart or a rope.
items.cn: 中古英语保留了这个动词，并把词义从「揪」扩大到任何持续拖拽的动作，包括拉车、拉绳。

items.en: By the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries the noun pull appears beside the verb, naming the act and later the force itself.
items.cn: 到十六、十七世纪，名词 pull 出现在动词旁边，先指拉这个动作，后来指拉力本身。

items.en: Modern English uses pull for drawing, extracting, straining a muscle, physical attraction, and social influence, and keeps it in dozens of phrasal verbs.
items.cn: 现代英语用 pull 表示拉、拔出、拉伤肌肉、物理吸引与社会影响力，并让它出现在大量短语动词中。

note.en: The look-alike group collects short words that differ from pull by one sound or letter; the near-meaning group collects other verbs for moving something by force.
note.cn: 形近组收与 pull 只差一个音或一个字母的短词；近义组收其他表示「用力移动某物」的动词。
