entries.definitionCN: 一小片静水，或共同凑集的一笔钱。

entries.definition: The adult male of cattle.
entries.definitionCN: 成年的公牛。

entries.definition: The soft wet mass of crushed fruit or paper fibre.
entries.definitionCN: 压碎的水果或纸纤维形成的软浆。

entries.definition: A cloth spread over a coffin, or a gloom that settles on a place.
entries.definitionCN: 覆盖棺木的布，或笼罩某地的阴郁气氛。

entries.definition: To pull something heavy along a surface with effort.
entries.definitionCN: 费力地把沉重的东西沿地面拉动。

entries.definition: To pull something sharply and briefly.
entries.definitionCN: 猛地、短暂地拉一下。

entries.definition: To pull or carry something heavy over a distance.
entries.definitionCN: 把沉重的东西拖拉或搬运一段距离。

entries.definition: To pull something with a sudden hard movement.
entries.definitionCN: 猛地一拽。

normalIntro.en: The word is a short Germanic verb for closing a hand on something and drawing it back, and its family keeps that backward motion.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是一个简短的日耳曼动词，指手攥住东西往后拽，它的同族词都保留着这股向后的力道。

normal.en: Pull goes back to Old English pullian, to pluck or tug, and it never needed a Latin ancestor.
normal.cn: pull 上溯到古英语 pullian（揪、拽），它从来不需要一个拉丁祖先。

normal.en: Pull out, pull up and pull over are phrasal verbs: the particle tells you which direction the drawing goes.
normal.cn: pull out、pull up、pull over 都是短语动词，小品词告诉你拉力朝哪个方向。

normal.en: Pull a muscle is the same motion turned inward, because the fibres are drawn apart inside the leg.
normal.cn: pull a muscle 是把同一个动作转向身体内部，因为腿里的纤维被拽开了。

normal.en: Pullover is a garment you pull over your head, so the compound keeps the original gesture in plain sight.
normal.cn: pullover 是从头上拉下去穿的衣服，复合词把原来的动作明明白白留在里面。

normal.en: The noun pull can mean influence, because a person who can draw decisions is doing what a rope does to a load.
normal.cn: 名词 pull 能指影响力，因为能牵动决定的人，做的正是绳子对货物做的事。

abstract.en: A pull is a relationship: something on one end always answers to something on the other.
abstract.cn: 拉是一种关系：一端的东西总是在回应另一端。

abstract.en: English lets one short verb cover rope, tooth, muscle and reputation, because all four resist and then give way.
abstract.cn: 英语让一个短动词同时覆盖绳子、牙齿、肌肉和名声，因为这四样都会先抵抗、然后松脱。

abstract.en: What draws a person is not so different from what draws a boat: a force outside, and a rope that holds.
abstract.cn: 吸引一个人的力量和拉动一条船的力量相差不大：外面一股力，中间一根绳。

examples.en: He pulled the chair closer to the fire.
examples.cn: 他把椅子拉近火边。

examples.en: The nurse pulled the sheet back to check the wound.
examples.cn: 护士把床单拉开查看伤口。

examples.en: She felt the pull of the old town and went back.
examples.cn: 她感受到老城的吸引力，于是回去了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「扑」——人往前一扑，抓住东西就往回拽，记住 pull 是拉。

root: 古英语 pullian（揪、拽），属日耳曼语层，无可靠拉丁同族词；由「手攥住往后拽」这一动作，发展出拔出、拉伤、拉力、吸引力与影响力诸义。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a hand closing on something and drawing it back; the senses divide into moving a whole object, extracting a part, straining a muscle, the force itself, and social leverage.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「手攥住东西往回拽」；义项由此分为移动整个物体、取出其中一部分、拉伤肌肉、力本身，以及社会上的影响力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands gripping a thick rope, feet braced on the ground, drawing it back inch by inch.
core.cn: 核心意象：双手攥住粗绳，双脚蹬地，一寸寸把绳子拽回来。

branches.en: a door dragged open against a stiff hinge
branches.cn: 顶着发涩的合页把门拽开

branches.en: a tooth eased out of its socket
branches.cn: 一颗牙从牙槽里被取出来

branches.en: a runner stopping short with a torn calf
branches.cn: 短跑者突然停下，小腿拉伤

branches.en: the moon lifting a whole sea
branches.cn: 月亮把整片海拉起来

branches.en: a name that opens doors without a key
branches.cn: 一个不用钥匙就能开门的名字

intro.en: The word is held together by an Old English verb of plucking, the English verb itself, two native suffixes, and three compounds built on the same gesture.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示「揪、拽」的古英语动词、英语动词本身、两个本族后缀，以及三个建立在同一动作上的复合词共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: one who pulls, or a pulling tool
a garment pulled over the head
a withdrawal to an earlier position
an exercise of pulling the body up

definition_zh: 苍白的；浅色的；逊色的；变苍白
definition_en: having little colour in the face, light and weak in shade, less impressive than something it is compared with, and to lose colour
core_image: 一张血色退去的脸，像被水冲淡的颜色
scene: 清晨的诊室里，医生抬起病人的手腕，看那张几乎没有血色的脸。 The nurse noticed how pale his face had become after the long night.
sceneCN: 这里 pale 是「脸色苍白」（第 1 个义项：脸上缺少血色）；句意为护士注意到他熬过漫长一夜之后脸色变得多么苍白。图中可辨识物件：诊室的灯、病人的手腕、床尾的病历夹。

derivatives.zh: pale 加表示性质的后缀 -ness，指苍白、色淡
pale 加副词后缀 -ly，指苍白地、淡淡地
与 pale 同出拉丁语 pallor，指脸色苍白，多用于书面
与 pale 同出拉丁词干 pallidus，指无血色的、病态的苍白

senses.title: Having little colour in the face
senses.definition: having less colour than usual in the face, often because of illness, fear or tiredness
senses.definitionCN: 脸上比平时缺少血色，常因生病、害怕或疲惫
senses.example: She went pale when the results were read out.
senses.exampleCN: 结果念出来的时候，她的脸一下子白了。
senses.why: Latin pallere meant to be pale, and the word has always started from skin losing its healthy colour, so the face is its oldest and most natural subject.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 pallere 本义就是发白、失色，这个词最早说的是皮肤失去健康颜色，所以「脸」是它最古老也最自然的落点。

senses.title: Light and weak in shade
senses.definition: of a colour or light, close to white and not strong or deep
senses.definitionCN: 指颜色或光线接近白色，不浓、不深
senses.example: The walls were painted a pale grey.
senses.exampleCN: 墙被刷成了浅浅的灰色。
senses.why: Once the word names a weak version of white, it can describe any colour that has been diluted, which is why pale blue sits nearer white than pure blue.
senses.whyCN: 这个词一旦用来指「被冲淡的白」，就能描述任何掺淡的颜色，所以 pale blue 比纯蓝更靠近白。

senses.title: Weaker than what it is compared with
senses.definition: less impressive, less strong or less real than another thing of the same kind
senses.definitionCN: 比同类的另一事物更不打动人、更弱或更不真实
senses.example: The new version is a pale imitation of the old one.
senses.exampleCN: 新版本只是对旧版本一种拙劣的模仿。
senses.why: A pale copy lacks the full colour of the original, so the word came to mean anything that looks washed out beside a stronger model.
senses.whyCN: 淡色的复制品没有原件那样饱满的颜色，于是这个词转指任何在更强的样本旁显得褪色、单薄的东西。

senses.title: To lose colour from the face
senses.definition: to become pale, especially in the face, or to make something seem less strong by comparison
senses.definitionCN: 变得苍白，尤指脸色发白；也可指使某物相形之下显得黯淡
senses.example: His cheeks paled at the sight of the blood.
senses.exampleCN: 一看见血，他的双颊就白了。
senses.why: The verb only sets the adjective in motion: the colour leaves the face while others watch it go, so the change itself becomes the event.
senses.whyCN: 动词只是把形容词动了起来：血色在旁人眼前从脸上退走，于是「退去」这个变化本身成了一件可以叙述的事。

intro.en: Pale comes from Latin pallere, to be pale, through Old French; the same Latin family gives pallor and pallid, so the colour sense is very old.
intro.cn: pale 出自拉丁语 pallere（发白），经古法语进入英语；同一拉丁词族还给出 pallor 与 pallid，颜色义由来已久。

items.en: The verb pallere meant to be pale or to look colourless, and it described the skin before it described anything else.
items.cn: 动词 pallere 意为发白、没有血色，它最初描述的是皮肤，而不是别的物体。

items.en: Its adjective pallidus meant pale or wan and passed into learned words such as pallid.
items.cn: 它的形容词 pallidus 意为苍白、憔悴，后来进入 pallid 这类书面词。

items.en: Old French turned the Latin adjective into pale, and the form crossed to England with Norman French.
items.cn: 古法语把拉丁形容词写成 pale，这个形式随诺曼法语一起进入英格兰。

items.en: Middle English used pale for a face without colour and, by extension, for light and washed-out shades.
items.cn: 中古英语用 pale 指没有血色的脸，并由此延伸到浅淡、发白的颜色。

items.en: Modern English keeps paler and palest as the comparison, and adds the figurative sense of a weak or faded copy.
items.cn: 现代英语用 paler 与 palest 作比较级和最高级，并增加了「逊色、褪色的复制品」这一比喻义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the learned relatives that keep the Latin colour stem; the near-meaning group gathers words for a face or a shade that has lost its strength.
note.cn: 形近组收保留拉丁颜色词干的书面亲属词；近义组收描述失去强度的脸色与色调的词。

entries.definition: Pale and unhealthy, especially of a face; it keeps the Latin adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 苍白而病态的，尤指脸色；保留了拉丁形容词。

entries.definition: The state of being pale, used mostly in medical writing.
entries.definitionCN: 苍白的状态，多用于医学文字。

entries.definition: The quality of being pale; pale plus -ness.
entries.definitionCN: 苍白的性质；pale 加 -ness。

entries.definition: The colour of fresh snow or milk, the lightest shade there is.
entries.definitionCN: 新雪或牛奶的颜色，最浅的色调。

entries.definition: Pale and tired-looking, as if from illness.
entries.definitionCN: 苍白而疲惫的，像病后那样。

entries.definition: Pale grey, like ash, usually of a frightened face.
entries.definitionCN: 灰白的，像灰烬一样，常形容受惊的脸。

normalIntro.en: The word is built on a Latin verb for being pale, and everything else in the family returns to a colour that has been drained.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在拉丁语表示「发白」的动词上，词族里其余的词都回到一种被抽走浓度的颜色。

normal.en: Latin pallere means to be pale, so the word begins at the skin, not at the paint pot.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 pallere 意为发白，所以这个词的起点在皮肤，而不在油漆桶。

normal.en: Pallor and pallid are learned relatives that keep the Latin colour sense.
normal.cn: pallor 与 pallid 是保留拉丁颜色义的书面亲属词。

normal.en: A face goes pale, a colour is pale, and a copy looks pale beside the original: one word measures distance from full colour.
normal.cn: 脸会发白，颜色会发淡，复制品在原件旁显得褪色，同一个词量的是离饱满颜色有多远。

normal.en: The verb pale is simply the adjective set in motion while others watch the colour leave.
normal.cn: 动词 pale 只是把形容词动起来，让别人看着颜色退走。

normal.en: Pale blue is not a kind of blue but blue with white mixed in, which is why the word can also mean weak.
normal.cn: pale blue 不是一种蓝，而是掺了白的蓝，所以这个词也能表示「弱」。

abstract.en: Colour is evidence of health, so losing it is the body's first way of saying that something is wrong.
abstract.cn: 颜色是健康的证据，褪色是身体最先说出「不对劲」的方式。

abstract.en: A pale copy is judged against an original it cannot match, which turns the word into a quiet comparison.
abstract.cn: 淡色的复制品总被拿去和配不上的原件相比，这个词因此成了一场安静的对照。

abstract.en: Every pale thing is a full thing with part of its colour taken away.
abstract.cn: 每个发淡的东西，都是被抽走了一部分颜色的完整之物。

examples.en: She went pale when the results were read out.
examples.cn: 结果念出来的时候，她的脸一下子白了。

examples.en: The walls were painted a pale grey.
examples.cn: 墙被刷成了浅浅的灰色。

examples.en: The sequel is a pale copy of the original film.
examples.cn: 这部续集是原片一个褪色的复制品。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「陪」——病人脸色苍白，床边总得有人陪着；记住 pale 是苍白。

root: 拉丁语 pallere（发白）— pallidus（苍白的）— 古法语 pale — 英语 pale；同族书面词有 pallor、pallid。

sensesIntro.en: The core is colour with its strength taken out; the senses move from the face, to light shades, to the figurative weak copy, and finally to the act of losing colour.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是被抽走浓度的颜色；义项从脸，到浅淡的色彩，再到比喻性的「逊色复制品」，最后回到「失去颜色」这个动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a face whose colour has drained away like paint thinned by water.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张血色退去的脸，颜色像被水冲淡的颜料。

branches.en: a patient's face under a clinic lamp
branches.cn: 诊室灯下病人的脸

branches.en: a wall painted a soft grey
branches.cn: 被刷成柔和浅灰的墙

branches.en: a sequel that cannot match the first film
branches.cn: 比不过首部的续集

branches.en: cheeks losing colour at the sight of blood
branches.cn: 见到血时退去血色的脸颊

branches.en: a washed-out colour and a washed-out copy
branches.cn: 褪掉的颜色与褪掉的复制品

intro.en: The word is carried by a Latin verb of being pale, its adjective and noun, and English suffixes that turn the quality into a state or a manner.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语表示发白的动词及其形容词、名词承载，再加上把性质变成状态或方式的英语后缀。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is well recorded: a verb of being pale, an adjective for the pale colour, and a noun for paleness itself.
latinIntro.cn: 这一拉丁词族有明确记录：表示发白的动词、指苍白颜色的形容词，以及指苍白本身的名词。

items.meaning: to be pale, to lack colour

definition_zh: 页；书页；网页；页面；呼叫；翻页
definition_en: one side of a sheet in a book or newspaper, a screen of content on a website, or to call out a name in a public place
core_image: 书页一角被风掀起，露出上一行还没读完的字
scene: 午后的阅览室里，风扇把摊开的书吹得轻轻翻动。 He turned the page and found a note in the margin.
sceneCN: 这里 page 是「书页」（第 1 个义项：书本或报纸的一面）；句意是他翻过这一页，在页边空白处发现一行批注。图中可辨识的物件：摊开的书、风扇、页边批注。

collocations.zh: 翻过这一页；翻开新的一页
让人一页接一页读下去的

derivatives.zh: 由 page 加 -ing 构成，指广播或设备里的分页呼叫
由 page 加表示工具或人的后缀 -er 构成，指寻呼机
由拉丁 pagina（页）加动词后缀 -ate 构成，义为「给……编页码」
由 paginate 加 -ion 构成，义为「页码编排」

senses.title: One side of a sheet in a book or newspaper
senses.definition: one side of a single sheet of paper in a book, magazine or newspaper
senses.definitionCN: 书、杂志或报纸中一张纸的一面
senses.example: She dog-eared the page to mark her place.
senses.exampleCN: 她把那一页折了个角，标住自己读到哪儿。
senses.why: Latin pagina named the column of writing on a papyrus sheet, so the word began as the surface that carries text rather than the sheet itself.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 pagina 本指纸草上书写的一栏文字，所以这个词最初指承载文字的那一面，而不是整张纸。

senses.title: A screen of content on a website
senses.definition: a single screen of content that a browser loads from a website
senses.definitionCN: 浏览器从网站载入的一屏内容
senses.example: The error page told us the link had expired.
senses.exampleCN: 那个错误页面提示我们链接已经失效。
senses.why: When text moved from paper to glass, the old word for a readable surface was simply carried over to what a browser shows.
senses.whyCN: 文字从纸面搬到玻璃屏上之后，人们就把这个表示「可读表面」的旧词直接搬去指浏览器显示的内容。

senses.title: To call a name out over a speaker
senses.definition: to call someone's name through a loudspeaker or an electronic device in order to reach them
senses.definitionCN: 通过扩音器或电子设备呼叫某人的名字，以便找到对方
senses.example: The airport staff paged her twice before she heard it.
senses.exampleCN: 机场工作人员呼叫了她两次，她才听见。
senses.why: This sense is usually said to come from the page who ran messages in a household; sending a name out to find a person survived after the servant vanished.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项一般认为来自旧时在宅院里跑腿传话的侍童；侍童消失了，但「把名字传出去找人」的做法留了下来。

senses.title: To look through a book page by page
senses.definition: to turn the pages of a book or magazine quickly while looking at them
senses.definitionCN: 快速翻动书或杂志的页面，一边翻一边看
senses.example: He paged through the atlas while waiting.
senses.exampleCN: 他等的时候一页页翻着那本地图册。
senses.why: The verb only turns the noun into an action: if a page is the unit of a book, then to page is to move through those units.
senses.whyCN: 动词只是把名词变成动作：既然页是书的单位，那么翻页就是沿着这些单位一路往下走。

intro.en: Page goes back to a Latin noun for a column of writing, and English later used the same word for servants, web screens and loudspeaker calls.
intro.cn: page 可追到拉丁语中表示「书写的一栏」的名词，英语后来用同一个词指侍从、网页和广播呼叫。

items.en: Pagina meant a column of writing on a papyrus roll, and it is generally thought to come from the verb pangere.
items.cn: pagina 指纸草卷上的一栏文字，一般认为出自动词 pangere。

items.en: Pangere meant to fasten or plant, and the link to writing is usually explained as lines fixed onto a surface.
items.cn: pangere 意为固定、插下；它与书写的联系，一般认为是指一行行字被「固定」在表面上。

items.en: Old French page named both a leaf of a book and a young servant, and English took over both meanings.
items.cn: 古法语 page 既指书的一页，也指年轻的侍从，英语把这两个意思都接了过来。

items.en: Middle English page kept the book sense and the servant sense side by side for centuries.
items.cn: 中古英语的 page 让「书页」和「侍从」两个意思并行了好几百年。

items.en: Modern English added the newspaper page, the web page, and the verbs for calling a name and turning pages.
items.cn: 现代英语又添上报纸版面、网页，以及「呼叫名字」和「翻页」的动词用法。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms built on the Latin stem for a written column; the near-meaning group collects words for paper leaves and for calling someone.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在「书写的一栏」这一拉丁词干上的形式；近义组收表示纸页和呼唤某人的词。

entries.definition: The Latin noun for a column of writing, the source of the English word.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语中表示书写栏目的名词，是英语这个词的来源。

entries.definition: To number the pages of a document.
entries.definitionCN: 给文件的各页编上页码。

entries.definition: A small device that beeps when someone is trying to reach you.
entries.definitionCN: 有人找你时会响的小型设备；寻呼机。

entries.definition: A public show with costumes and scenes; it is only close in spelling, and its source is different.
entries.definitionCN: 有服装和场景的公开演出；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A single piece of paper, or one side of it.
entries.definitionCN: 一张纸，或纸的一面。

entries.definition: A sheet of paper in a book, especially when numbered on both sides.
entries.definitionCN: 书中一张纸，尤指两面都编了号的。

entries.definition: What a device shows at one time.
entries.definitionCN: 设备一次显示的内容；屏幕。

entries.definition: To call someone to come, often officially.
entries.definitionCN: 召唤某人前来，常带正式意味。

normalIntro.en: Page began as the written surface of a roll, and its family keeps two ideas alive: numbered leaves and calling a name out.
normalIntro.cn: page 最初指卷轴上书写的那一面，同族词一直保有两个想法：编了号的纸页，以及把名字喊出去。

normal.en: Latin pagina is the written column, so page is first a surface that holds text.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 pagina 是书写的一栏，所以 page 首先是承载文字的表面。

normal.en: Pangere means to fasten, which is why pagina is often explained as lines fixed onto a surface.
normal.cn: pangere 意为固定，所以一般认为 pagina 就是被固定在表面上的一行行字。

normal.en: The suffix -ate in paginate turns the noun into a verb: to give a document its page numbers.
normal.cn: paginate 里的后缀 -ate 把名词变成动词，意思是给文件编上页码。

normal.en: The servant sense survives in the verb to page someone, because a page carried messages by name.
normal.cn: 「侍从」这个意思留在动词 to page 里，因为侍从就是按名字替人传话的。

normal.en: Web page puts the old word on a new surface, so the meaning moves from paper to screen without changing its core.
normal.cn: 网页只是把这个旧词放到新的表面上，词义从纸移到屏幕，核心并没有变。

abstract.en: A page is a unit small enough to finish, which is why turning the page can mean starting over.
abstract.cn: 一页小到能读完，所以「翻过这一页」也可以表示重新开始。

abstract.en: Numbering pages makes a book addressable: any sentence can be found again later.
abstract.cn: 给页编号让整本书可以被定位：任何一句话以后都能重新找到。

abstract.en: One word covers paper, screens and loudspeaker calls because all three put a name or a text where someone can meet it.
abstract.cn: 同一个词覆盖纸、屏幕和广播，因为这三者都是把名字或文字放到别人能遇上的地方。

examples.en: He turned the page and found a note in the margin.
examples.cn: 他翻过这一页，在页边发现一行批注。

examples.en: The site's help page explains how to reset the password.
examples.cn: 网站的帮助页面说明了如何重设密码。

examples.en: The nurse paged the doctor at midnight.
examples.cn: 护士在午夜呼叫了医生。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「佩奇」——翻开书页，小猪佩奇正坐在页码上；page 是书页，也是呼叫。

root: 拉丁语 pagina（书写的一栏）一般认为出自 pangere（固定、钉住），经古法语 page 进入英语；同族词多与纸页、编号有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core image is a written surface you can turn; from it come the book page, the web page, the act of turning pages, and the call that sends a name out.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心意象是一面可以翻动的书写表面；书页、网页、翻页的动作，以及把名字喊出去的呼叫，都由此展开。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the corner of a page lifting in a breeze, showing the line above it.
core.cn: 核心意象：书页一角被风掀起，露出上一行还没读完的字。

branches.en: a reader folding a corner to keep the place
branches.cn: 读者折起页角记住读到哪儿

branches.en: a browser showing the same old word on glass
branches.cn: 浏览器把同一个旧词显示在玻璃屏上

branches.en: a thumb moving quickly along the edge of a magazine
branches.cn: 拇指沿着杂志边缘快速翻动

branches.en: a voice repeating a name through a ceiling speaker
branches.cn: 声音通过天花板上的喇叭重复一个名字

branches.en: a paperless notice that still calls itself a page
branches.cn: 一份没有纸的通知仍然自称页面

intro.en: The word rests on the Latin noun pagina and the verb pangere, with English endings that produce a device and a numbering verb.
intro.cn: 这个词依托拉丁名词 pagina 与动词 pangere，再加上英语词尾，生出设备名和表示编号的动词。

latinIntro.en: Pagina, the Latin noun for a column of writing, and pangere, the verb to fasten, stand behind the English word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语名词 pagina（书写的一栏）与动词 pangere（固定）是英语这个词背后的来源。

items.meaning: column of writing on a roll
a leaf of a book; a young servant

derivatives.zh: 由 page 加 -er 构成，指寻呼机
由 paginate 加 -ion 构成，指页码编排
由 page 与 turner 复合而成，指让人一口气读完的书

definition_zh: 卷曲的；卷发的
definition_en: having curls or a curving round shape
core_image: 一圈一圈绕起来的小弹簧
scene: 新转来的同学顶着一头蓬蓬的头发，像顶着一朵云。 My little sister was born with soft curly hair.
sceneCN: 这里 curly 是「卷曲的」（第 1 个义项：头发一圈圈卷起来的样子）；句意是我妹妹生来就有一头柔软的卷发。

derivatives.zh: curly 的基础词，义为「卷毛；卷曲状」；作动词指「（使）卷曲」
由 curly 加 haired 构成，义为「卷发的」

senses.title: Hair that grows in ringlets
senses.definition: hair that grows in small round twists instead of hanging straight
senses.definitionCN: 头发长成一圈圈的小弯，而不是直直垂下
senses.example: The barber cut his curly hair very short for summer.
senses.exampleCN: 理发师把他的卷发剪得很短过夏天。
senses.why: A curl is a small round twist, and hair that twists all over is called curly.
senses.whyCN: curl 是一圈小弯，头发到处都是这种小弯，就叫 curly。

senses.title: Things shaped in curves
senses.definition: having a winding or coiled shape, like fur, tails or fries
senses.definitionCN: 呈弯绕或盘卷形状，如毛发、尾巴、薯条
senses.example: The little dog has curly fur all over its back.
senses.exampleCN: 小狗背上长满了卷卷的毛。
senses.why: Any coiled surface looks like a row of curls, so the word spread to fur and shapes.
senses.whyCN: 任何盘卷的表面都像一排小卷，于是这个词扩展到毛发和形状。

intro.en: Curly comes from curl, a word of uncertain early origin.
intro.cn: curly 来自 curl，而 curl 的早期来源尚不确定。

items.en: The verb curlen appeared, meaning to curl or to ripple.
items.cn: 中古英语出现 curlen，意为卷曲、起波纹。

items.en: It is generally thought to come from a Germanic source meaning to twist or coil; the exact form is uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为它源自一个意为扭转、盘绕的日耳曼语词，具体形式不确定。

items.en: The noun curl named a ringlet of hair or a ripple of water.
items.cn: 中古英语名词 curl 指发卷或水波纹。

items.en: The adjective curly formed with the -y suffix, first about hair, later about any coiled shape.
items.cn: 加 -y 后缀构成形容词 curly，先形容头发，后泛指任何盘卷形状。

items.en: Today curly describes hair, fur, leaves and even snack food.
items.cn: 如今 curly 可形容头发、皮毛、叶子甚至零食。

note.en: These words describe twisted shapes or opposite hair types.
note.cn: 这些词形容盘卷的形状或相反的发质。

entries.definition: a ringlet of hair; to twist into a curve
entries.definitionCN: 发卷；卷曲（动词）

entries.definition: twisted into curls
entries.definitionCN: 卷成圈的

entries.definition: having curly hair
entries.definitionCN: 卷发的

entries.definition: to throw with force; only spelled close to curl, unrelated
entries.definitionCN: 猛投（拼写近似 curl，词义无关）

entries.definition: hair with gentle waves, less tight than curls
entries.definitionCN: 波浪形的

entries.definition: wound into rings, like a spring
entries.definitionCN: 盘绕的

entries.definition: turned into a spiral shape
entries.definitionCN: 拧成螺旋的

entries.definition: hair hanging flat without curls
entries.definitionCN: 直的

entries.definition: hair with many small uncontrolled curls
entries.definitionCN: 毛躁卷曲的

normalIntro.en: Build the word from curl plus the adjective ending.
normalIntro.cn: 从 curl 加形容词词尾来拼这个词。

normal.en: curl + y = curly, full of curls.
normal.cn: curl（卷）+ y ＝ curly（多卷的）。

normal.en: curl also names a small ringlet: a lock, a wave, a spring.
normal.cn: curl 也指小卷：发卷、波纹、弹簧圈。

normal.en: Compare straight hair with curly hair when describing classmates.
normal.cn: 描述同学时对比 straight hair（直发）与 curly hair（卷发）。

normal.en: Spelling: curl like the word for a ringlet, then add y.
normal.cn: 拼写：先写 curl（卷曲），再加 y。

normal.en: curly fries are potato strips twisted into springs.
normal.cn: curly fries（卷卷薯条）是拧成弹簧状的土豆条。

abstract.en: Picture a tiny spring bouncing in each strand of hair.
abstract.cn: 想象每根头发里都藏着一个小弹簧。

abstract.en: Draw the letter c many times; each c is one curl.
abstract.cn: 连画许多个字母 c，每个 c 就是一个小卷。

abstract.en: Feel the bouncy softness of a poodle's coat.
abstract.cn: 体会贵宾犬毛发蓬松有弹性的手感。

examples.en: Her curly hair bounces when she runs in PE class.
examples.cn: 她跑操时卷发一颠一颠的。

examples.en: The baby has big blue eyes and curly hair.
examples.cn: 这个婴儿有大大的蓝眼睛和卷卷的头发。

examples.en: I ordered curly fries at the new snack shop.
examples.cn: 我在新开的零食店点了卷卷薯条。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「可理」——卷发要「可劲儿理」也理不直，因为它是 curly

root: curl 的来源一般认为出自日耳曼语系表示「扭转、盘绕」的词（具体形式存疑），中古英语写作 curlen；加形容词后缀 -y 构成 curly，指「多卷的」。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts with ringlets of hair and stretches to any coiled shape.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从发卷出发，延伸到任何盘卷的形状。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small spring twisted round and round
core.cn: 核心意象：一圈一圈绕起来的小弹簧

branches.en: Ringlets growing from the head
branches.cn: 头上长出的一圈圈发卷

branches.en: Fur, tails and leaves in curves
branches.cn: 卷毛、卷尾、卷叶等弯曲形状

branches.en: Anything that twists into rings
branches.cn: 凡是拧成一圈圈的东西

branches.en: Food twisted into springs
branches.cn: 拧成弹簧状的食物

branches.en: The opposite of straight hair
branches.cn: 与直发相对

intro.en: Curly is a simple adjective made from curl plus y.
intro.cn: curly 是由 curl 加 y 构成的简单形容词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root here; the family is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁词根，词族属于日耳曼语系。

items.exampleCN: 「a curl fell on her forehead」，一缕发卷垂在额头

items.example: her hair curlen in the damp
items.exampleCN: （中古英语用法）潮湿中头发打卷
coil the rope（把绳子盘起来）

items.meaning: a wire twisted into rings that bounces

definition_zh: 孙女；外孙女
definition_en: the daughter of one's son or daughter
core_image: 隔一代的女儿：你孩子生的女孩，扎着辫子跑进家门
scene: 外婆把新织的红毛衣摊在膝上比了比尺寸。 Her granddaughter is learning to knit too.
sceneCN: 这里 granddaughter 是「孙女」（第 1 个义项：子女的女儿）；句意为她的孙女也在学织毛线。

pos.zh: 名词：孙女；外孙女（特指女性孙辈）

derivatives.zh: 不分性别的上位词，指孙辈
对应的男性孙辈词
复合词来源词，指女儿

senses.title: A daughter of your child
senses.definition: a girl child of your son or daughter
senses.definitionCN: 你儿子或你女儿所生的女孩
senses.example: His granddaughter drew him a birthday card.
senses.exampleCN: 他的孙女给他画了一张生日卡。
senses.why: The core image is the second-generation daughter: grand plus daughter.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是隔一代的女儿：grand 加 daughter。

senses.title: A treasured young girl outside strict kinship
senses.definition: a young girl treated with grandparent-like affection though not a blood grandchild
senses.definitionCN: 虽无血缘却受到祖辈般疼爱的女孩
senses.example: The old teacher calls every pupil her granddaughter.
senses.exampleCN: 老教师把每个学生都称作自己的孙女。
senses.why: Affection lifts the kinship word beyond blood, just as elders adopt the young.
senses.whyCN: 长辈把年轻人认作自家孙辈，亲情使称谓越过了血缘边界。

intro.en: Granddaughter stacks the borrowed grand- over the native daughter.
intro.cn: granddaughter 把借来的 grand- 叠在本族 daughter 之上。

items.en: Latin grandis meant large or fully grown.
items.cn: 拉丁语 grandis 意为大、成年。

items.en: Old French grand entered English family words.
items.cn: 古法语 grand 进入英语家庭称谓。

items.en: Old English dohtor meant daughter, with a Germanic plural.
items.cn: 古英语 dohtor 指女儿，有日耳曼式复数。

items.en: Daughter settled in spelling while grand- spread into kinship terms.
items.cn: 中古英语 daughter 拼写定型，grand- 扩散到亲属词。

items.en: Granddaughter became the standard word for a female grandchild.
items.cn: 现代英语 granddaughter 成为女性孙辈的标准词。

note.en: Gender makes the grand- family branch cleanly.
note.cn: 性别让 grand- 家族干净地分了叉。

entries.definition: more than one granddaughter
entries.definitionCN: granddaughter 的复数

entries.definition: a niece's or nephew's child; shares grand-
entries.definitionCN: 侄孙辈；共用 grand-

entries.definition: magnificent quality from the same Latin root
entries.definitionCN: 宏伟；来自同一拉丁词根

entries.definition: the gender-neutral umbrella word
entries.definitionCN: 不分性别的上位词

entries.definition: the male counterpart
entries.definitionCN: 对应的男性孙辈

entries.definition: a brother's or sister's daughter, one generation closer
entries.definitionCN: 侄女或外甥女，血缘近一代

normalIntro.en: Five hooks for the girl on the family tree.
normalIntro.cn: 家族树上女孩的五条钩子。

normal.en: Granddaughter is grand + daughter, said fast.
normal.cn: granddaughter 就是 grand 加 daughter 的连读。

normal.en: Daughter gives the -ughter ending to remember.
normal.cn: 记住 -ughter 结尾来自 daughter。

normal.en: An eldest granddaughter often leads the cousins.
normal.cn: 大孙女常当表兄妹们的头。

normal.en: Grandparents knit sweaters for their granddaughters.
normal.cn: 祖辈给孙女们织毛衣。

normal.en: Say grandson, granddaughter, and you cover all grandchildren.
normal.cn: 说出 grandson、granddaughter 就覆盖了所有孙辈。

abstract.en: A granddaughter is tomorrow wearing yesterday's smile.
abstract.cn: 孙女是穿着昨日笑容的明天。

abstract.en: The family photo gains a new bright face.
abstract.cn: 家庭合影多了一张明亮的新脸。

abstract.en: Two generations hold hands in one word.
abstract.cn: 一个词里两代人牵手。

examples.en: Her granddaughter plays the violin every evening.
examples.cn: 她的孙女每晚拉小提琴。

examples.en: The old man walked his granddaughter to school.
examples.cn: 老人送孙女上学。

examples.en: Both my granddaughters were born in May.
examples.cn: 我的两个孙女都出生在五月。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「歌兰朵特」——隔一代的花朵尤其特别；granddaughter 就是家里的隔代花朵

root: grand（拉丁 grandis「大」，表隔一代）+ daughter（古英语 dohtor「女儿」）；复合称谓词，无拉丁直系后缀。

sensesIntro.en: One precise kinship sense: the female second-generation child.
sensesIntro.cn: 单一精确义项：隔一代的女性孩子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the girl standing one generation away
core.cn: 核心意象：隔一代站立的女孩

branches.en: daughter of my child
branches.cn: 我孩子的女儿

branches.en: the female branch of grandchild
branches.cn: grandchild 的女性分支

branches.en: the cherished young face
branches.cn: 被珍爱的年轻面孔

branches.en: the link across generations
branches.cn: 跨代际的纽带

branches.en: the mirror of grandson
branches.cn: grandson 的镜像词

intro.en: Granddaughter is a textbook grand- compound.
intro.cn: granddaughter 是典型的 grand- 复合词。

latinIntro.en: Only grand- carries Latin blood; daughter is native.
latinIntro.cn: 只有 grand- 带拉丁血统；daughter 是本族的。

items.example: The baby granddaughter slept in the cradle.
